A vision-capable language model with a fixed output schema handles this variety. Each row carries a confidence score and a highlight of the exact source text, owner corrections feed the alias table, and nothing the AI produces becomes an order without passing the rules and a human approval.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: The user never chats with it. The AI is an invisible extraction step that outputs a table with confidence badges, measured against a labelled synthetic test set. What the user works with is a supplier comparison grid, a list of spikes, a buy plan with RM savings, and an approve button that sends orders. Judges will see a document-to-decision pipeline, the same category as invoice OCR feeding procurement rules, not a reskinned chat assistant. It also fails safe: low-confidence lines go to a human queue, not into a generated reply.
ideas.human_approval:
The consequential action is sending purchase orders to suppliers, which commits money.
- The purchaser role (head cook Ahmad) confirms or corrects low-confidence lines. In the example he confirms that 'cili merah 18' means RM18.00/kg. He may approve routine plans of RM300 or less that keep every line with the usual supplier.
- The owner role (Kak Yati) must approve any plan over RM300, any supplier switch, any new supplier and any substitution.

On the approval screen she sees:
- each extracted price next to a crop of its source message or photo, with its confidence
- the per-line comparison across suppliers and the chosen supplier
- spike flags with lever options
- the plan total and the saving against the usual suppliers (RM15.80)
- which constraints applied (ayam locked to Pak Mat)
- the exact order message each supplier will receive
She can untick a switch, for example keeping sawi with Ah Seng to protect credit terms, and the totals update live before she approves.
ideas.roles_and_permissions:
RBAC is simulated with a role switcher.
- Owner: sees all prices, history and savings. Manages suppliers, locks, approval limits and the substitution list. Approves plans over RM300, switches and new suppliers.
- Purchaser or head cook: forwards messages, confirms extraction lines, edits order quantities within the par range, and approves routine plans of RM300 or less with usual suppliers only. Cannot add suppliers or change limits.
- Kitchen or receiving staff: tick delivered quantities and photograph delivery invoices. Cannot see the supplier comparison.
- Bookkeeper: read-only access to orders and price history.
- Suppliers: no access. They only receive the approved order message.
ideas.outcome_and_log:
After approval, the system generates one order message per supplier from a template in that supplier's language. For example: '老板，明天要：菜心 12公斤，辣椒 4公斤。谢谢 - Dapur Kak Yati'. Each is sent through a wa.me click-to-chat link, or simulated as sent in the demo. The user sees the order status per supplier, an updated price history chart per ingredient, and a running counter of 'saved vs usual this month'. Next morning the receiving staff tick quantities. Roadmap: the delivery invoice photo is read by the same extractor, and any line invoiced above its quoted price is flagged as an overcharge.

Activity log, append-only:
- '21:42 Message from Ah Seng parsed: 5 lines, 4 auto, 1 needs check'
- '21:50 Ahmad (Purchaser) confirmed cili merah 18 = RM18.00/kg; alias saved'
- '22:00 Plan built: 3 suppliers, saving RM15.80 vs usual, 1 spike flag'
- '22:06 Kak Yati (Owner) approved; kept bawang merah with Ah Seng'
- '22:06 Orders sent (simulated)'
Each entry links back to the source message.
ideas.measurable_benefit:
All figures are estimates to validate with pilot owners.
- Money: in the synthetic example, splitting the order saves RM15.80 a day, about RM410 a month over 26 trading days, against buying everything from the usual supplier. Real savings depend on how far supplier prices differ. Price swings are large and fast: sawi moved from RM2.50-3 to RM6-7/kg in two months (NST, 10 Dec 2025). SMEs already respond by 'seeking alternative suppliers', and 20% cite rising supplier costs (Airwallex SME Outlook via The Star, 1 Oct 2026, https://www.thestar.com.my/business/business-news/2026/10/01/rising-costs-top-concern-for-malaysian-smes-as-growth-remains-priority).
- Spoilage and stock-out: spike flags plus par-based quantities support the existing 1-2-days-of-stock habit without over-buying. This benefit is qualitative and to be measured in a pilot.
- Time: reading and comparing 3 supplier lists each night drops from about 20-30 minutes to about 5 minutes of review. This is an assumption.
- Accuracy KPIs: at least 95% of lines extracted correctly on a 50-message synthetic test set covering English, BM and Chinese; 100% of lines below 0.85 confidence routed to a human; zero orders sent without approval.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse:
It reuses Orbyte's approval-with-audit-trail engine, roles and org structure. It is a procurement-side module, and Orbyte currently lists no inventory or procurement. Approved orders and confirmed invoices can later be pushed to the accounting and payroll partners in Orbyte Connect as supplier bills, and they add supplier and payment-term nodes to the stated 'Business Graph'.

The extraction step works like the AI receipt reading Orbyte already ships in eClaim. Whether that component can be shared is unverified and depends on Orbyte's internals.

Reusable building block: a 'Document-to-Price API' (POST /supplier-documents returning normalised price rows with confidence), plus a 'Buy Plan' rules service with per-tenant constraints. The schema is not F&B-specific (item, pack size, unit, price, validity, minimum order), so the same module serves:
- hardware shops comparing cement and paint price lists
- car workshops comparing parts quotes
- printing shops buying paper and ink
- small manufacturers buying resin, steel or packaging
Sector differences live in alias tables and constraint templates, not in code.
ideas.scope_check:
This is not HR or admin. It covers procurement and inventory buying. There are no real payments: it only sends order messages, and payment stays offline under the supplier's normal terms. There are no statutory filings. It does not give financial advice: it compares quoted prices against owner-set rules, and the owner approves every order and switch.

PDPA 2010 (as amended in 2024):
- The demo uses only synthetic messages and suppliers.
- In real use, supplier messages can contain personal data, such as a sole proprietor's name and phone number. Only the supplier's business name and the price lines are kept.
- Phone numbers and other non-price text are removed before the AI model is called.
- Raw images and messages are deleted after a set retention period (e.g. 90 days), while the structured prices are kept.
- Data is tenant-scoped with role-based access. Model calls use a no-training data setting, and the data processing is disclosed to the SME in its terms.
- No customer data is involved.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope:
Build the extraction-to-approval loop live.
1. Paste the 3 synthetic supplier messages (English/Manglish, BM, Chinese) and upload 1 handwritten-chit image.
2. Show the AI-extracted table with unit normalisation, confidence badges and source highlights. One line ('cili merah 18') lands in the confirm queue.
3. In the purchaser role, confirm it.
4. The rules engine builds the buy plan with per-line savings and a spike flag.
5. Switch to the owner role and approve.
6. Show the generated per-supplier order messages and the activity log.
Also ship a 50-message labelled synthetic test set with a script that prints extraction accuracy, which backs the accuracy claim, plus cached extraction JSON so the demo still runs if the model API fails.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback:
Hardest risk: extraction errors, especially a wrong unit or alias, leading to a bad buy decision. Mitigation:
- a strict output schema
- a confidence threshold of 0.85 that sends lines to the human queue
- sanity rules: reject or flag a price more than 3 times or less than a third of the 4-week average, and any unit not seen before
- the alias table learning from every correction
- a measured accuracy report on the synthetic test set
- never ordering without approval
Fallback when the model is down or unsure: a quick-entry grid pre-filled with yesterday's prices, so the purchaser only edits the changes. In the demo, cached results are used.

Second risk: some purchases are cash buys at the wet market with no message to read. Fallback: a one-line typed or voice-note entry ('kangkung 3 ikat 6 ringgit') feeds the same pipeline.

Third risk: owners value supplier relationships and credit terms over a few sen. Mitigation: supplier locks, the minimum-saving threshold before any switch is suggested, and the owner's ability to untick any switch.
ideas.business_model:
It fits Orbyte's usage-credit wallet with per-unit charging.
- Freemium: about 60 parsed supplier documents a month free.
- Usage: credits per parsed message or photo above the free tier.
- Premium: multiple outlets, more suppliers and the invoice-to-quote overcharge check.
- Partner, two-sided growth: suppliers and distributors get a free supplier-side view to publish structured price lists into the hub. This cuts extraction cost and makes them visible to more buying SMEs, and they could later pay for featured listing or order-routing fees. Accounting and POS partners receive confirmed supplier bills through Connect.
- Indicative price point to test: about RM20-40 a month equivalent in credits for a single outlet. This is our assumption, about 5-10% of the estimated monthly saving.
- Growth path: F&B and caterers, then hardware, auto parts and small manufacturers. Roadmap item: an opt-in, anonymised regional input-price index, subject to competition-law review.

ideas.name: TempahLock: order commitment gate (rules only)
ideas.one_liner: A rules-only gate in Orbyte that keeps a large WhatsApp order out of the kitchen, off the ingredient run and away from any new supplier's bank account until it has a real commitment and a named person has cleared every red flag. A consumer order needs deposit proof. A government or company order needs an LO verified through ePerolehan or the agency's official number.
ideas.target_user: Micro and small Malaysian food and gift makers that take orders on WhatsApp: caterers, bakeries, kuih and home food sellers, door-gift and souvenir shops, florists. Typically 1-15 people, where a helper or staff member takes orders and the owner decides. Busiest at Ramadan/Raya, CNY and school or office event seasons. Evidence of who gets hit: Perak, 7 reports from bakeries and caterers, about RM300,000 (FMT/Bernama 17-18 Mar 2026; Utusan and RTM say 'hampir RM300,000'). Miri, five small flower and gift traders, more than RM28,000 (The Vibes, 24 May 2026). Penampang, a caterer who made 150 lunch sets for a fake 'army officer' (MustShareNews, 5 Jun 2023).
ideas.trigger:
Three triggers, all automatic.
(1) Order event: a new order enters the order book at or above the owner's threshold (default RM500), or with delivery within 7 days. It can arrive by a simulated WhatsApp Business Platform webhook, a shared order-form link, or staff pasting the chat into Quick Add.
(2) Money-out event: someone creates a 'Pay supplier' request for a supplier not on the approved list.
(3) Daily 7am schedule: lists orders whose production starts today but still lack a commitment.

Synthetic example. 'Dapur Mak Long Catering & Kuih' (fictional, Ipoh, 4 staff) gets this at 9:12pm: 'Assalamualaikum puan, saya En. Hafiz dari Pejabat Pendidikan Daerah Bandar Mutiara (fictional). Nak tempah 300 set kuih raya utk majlis Khamis ni, total RM7,500. Tambah 300 kotak kurma sekali ya. Kurma tu puan ambil dari supplier panel kami, nanti saya bagi no. dia. LO saya hantar esok.'
The next day a second number writes: 'Kak, saya dari Kurma Emas Trading. 300 kotak Ajwa RM18,000, kena bayar 50% dulu RM9,000 ya, akaun Maybank a/n MOHD ALI BIN ...'
Control cases: 'Hi Kak, nak order 80 pcs kuih lapis for my mum's birthday Sat, can?' (RM240), and a RM650 wedding order.
ideas.connected_data:
From the Orbyte hub:
- Product catalogue with an alias list and unit costs, from a POS/e-commerce connector or a sheet import.
- Daily capacity and the production calendar.
- Client records and order history, from Orbyte clients & projects: past orders, paid-on-time count, no-shows.
- Deposit evidence: an uploaded transfer screenshot, or read-only payment status from a payments-and-collections partner through Orbyte Connect. It never initiates a payment.
- Approved supplier list with registered business names and bank-account names, from the accounting connector.
- Org roles: owner, second approver, staff, kitchen.
- The shop's own median order value and lead time, computed from history.
ideas.decision_logic:
Rules only. Each has a code and a one-line reason in BM and English.
- R1 Consumer commitment: a consumer order of RM300 or more needs deposit proof of at least 30% (owner-configurable) before it can move to Confirmed. No production slot is reserved before that. This automates sellers' own 'booking with payment' fix (Kosmo, 21 Apr 2023).
- R2 Government or company buyer: no deposit rule, because genuine government orders pay after delivery (MustShareNews, 2023: 'This is apparently how government orders work'). That avoids false positives. Instead the order needs either (a) the LO checked in the seller's own ePerolehan account, or (b) a callback to an official number taken from the agency's own website, recorded with where the number came from. Basis: KPWKM says its procurement runs only through ePerolehan and urges suppliers to check orders there (The Star QuickCheck, 5 Aug 2026). MOT says any purchase order 'that cannot be verified through official channels is not valid' (The Star, 2 Oct 2026).
- R3 Not our product: a line item that matches no catalogue SKU or alias is RED. This is the Perak MO, where extra items are 'usually ones not produced by the business operator'.
- R4 Buyer-named supplier: a supplier introduced by the buyer, or any supplier not on the approved list, is RED and locks supplier payment.
- R5 Payee mismatch: a bank-account name that differs from the supplier's business name is RED. This matches the mule-account pattern in Miri and Kuantan.
- R6 Rush and size: an order worth more than 3x the shop's median and due within 72 hours is AMBER.
- R7 Pay-to-confirm: any request for money to 'confirm', 'register' or 'secure' an order is RED. KPWKM: 'has never asked suppliers to make any payments'.

Outcome: any RED puts the order on HELD for the owner. AMBER sends it to owner review. GREEN lets staff confirm. Only the owner can override, and must type a reason.
In the example, the PPD order fires R2, R3, R4 and R6. The RM9,000 kurma request fires R4 and R5.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: AI is not needed and deliberately not used. Once the order is a card (items, buyer type, value, date, supplier, payee name), every check compares structured data against the shop's own catalogue, thresholds and supplier list. Rules make each hold explainable in one sentence and predictable for a non-technical owner. Item matching uses an owner-maintained alias list, for example 'kuih raya', 'biskut raya' and 'cookies raya' all map to one SKU. Roadmap only: optional AI to pre-fill the card from pasted chat, always shown for confirmation and never deciding. This is the deliberate contrast with concept 2.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no conversation and no AI. It is an order state machine (Draft, Awaiting commitment, Confirmed, Released to production, Delivered, Closed, plus Held and Rejected) with role-locked transitions. Judges see an approval queue, a kitchen board that shows only released orders, and an audit log. The value is enforcing the owner's own policy when the owner is busy, or when a helper takes the order at 9pm.
ideas.human_approval:
Release to production. The owner approves this for any order at or above the threshold, or with an AMBER or RED flag. The decision screen shows:
- the order card
- commitment evidence: deposit required vs received, with the screenshot; or the ePerolehan check result plus the callback record (who called, which number, where that number came from, who answered, when)
- every fired rule with its reason
- customer history
- ingredient cost at risk in RM and the capacity impact

Pay new supplier. The product only records the request; the transfer itself happens in the bank app. It needs two keys: the owner, plus a nominated second approver (business partner, spouse or bookkeeper, invited as a guest role). It also needs a recorded Semak Mule check of the account number and company name (semakmule.rmp.gov.my, free PDRM tool). Buyer-introduced suppliers get a 24-hour cooling-off.
Why two keys: in a 1-4 person firm the owner is the person being pressured, so the second key belongs to someone outside the WhatsApp conversation. A sole trader with no one to nominate gets the cooling-off plus a mandatory checklist instead.

Staff can never override a hold.
ideas.roles_and_permissions:
Simulated RBAC.
- Owner: full access. Edits rules and thresholds, approves release, overrides with a typed reason, holds the first key on supplier payments.
- Second approver (guest): sees held orders and supplier payment requests, holds the second key. Cannot edit orders or rules.
- Staff / order taker: creates orders, uploads deposit proof, records callbacks and Semak Mule results. Can confirm GREEN orders only. Cannot release HELD orders or add an unapproved supplier as payee.
- Kitchen / production: sees only released orders, with items, quantities, due date and pickup slot. No buyer phone numbers or payment data (PDPA minimisation).
- Bookkeeper (optional, read-only): deposits ledger and supplier payment requests, with export.
All data is tenant-isolated.
ideas.outcome_and_log:
What the user sees:
- a status chip on each order (HELD, 4 reasons / CONFIRMED / RELEASED)
- a kitchen board that lists only released orders
- a daily 'money at risk' panel: ingredient cost of held orders not yet started, supplier prepayments blocked, deposits outstanding

In the example, the PPD order is HELD. The owner calls the PPD number from its official website and is told there is no such order, so she marks it REJECTED with the reason 'impersonation suspected'. The RM9,000 kurma request never gets its two keys. The panel shows 'RM9,000 prepayment blocked; about RM2,100 ingredient cost not spent' (synthetic). The RM240 order goes green straight to the board. The RM650 wedding order confirms once the RM195 deposit screenshot is attached.

The activity log is append-only. It records:
- timestamp, actor, role, order ID, action, status before and after
- rules fired, with their inputs (for example R3: 'kurma 300 kotak' matched no SKU)
- evidence file hashes
- callback and Semak Mule records
- approvals, rejections and overrides, with typed reasons
- cooling-off start and end
It exports to CSV for the bookkeeper or as an evidence pack for a police report.
ideas.measurable_benefit:
All figures here are estimates. Per-victim averages are our own arithmetic on the reported totals.
Reported losses per incident:
- Miri: more than RM28,000 across five traders (about RM5,600 each)
- Kuantan: RM89,300 across five traders (about RM17,900 each)
- Perak: about RM300,000 across 7 reports (about RM43,000 each)
- Raub: RM315,963 for one printing shop
Estimate: stopping one such incident keeps RM5,000-RM45,000 for a typical micro victim. That outweighs years of subscription.
Estimate for consumer no-shows: the ingredient cost of each unpaid order prepared. Evidence here is thin and dated (RM300 doughnuts, SAYS 2022), so we treat it as a secondary benefit.
Pilot KPIs we can actually measure:
- share of orders above threshold with commitment evidence before production (target 100%; baseline unknown)
- share of new-supplier payment requests with two keys (target 100%)
- time to capture an order card (target under 60 s)
Honest framing: fraud hits any one business rarely. NST/CCID reports 241 cases nationally in 2025 for souvenir and food orders, and does not state victim size. The daily value is the order book and deposit discipline; the fraud gate works like insurance.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse:
Reuses existing Orbyte pieces:
- platform-wide review and approval with audit trail, roles, org structure
- clients & projects (buyer = client, order = project)
- optional eSign (Documenso), so the buyer can sign an order confirmation with deposit and cancellation terms
Connect usage:
- payments and collections: read deposit status only
- accounting: approved supplier list; approved supplier bills written back to the system of record, which matches Orbyte's write-back model
- POS and e-commerce: catalogue
It feeds Orbyte's stated Business Graph (orders, payment terms, cash flow) and fills white space: Orbyte has no orders, receivables or WhatsApp today.
Reusable 'Commitment Gate' module and API: POST /orders, POST /orders/{id}/evaluate (returns rule hits), POST /payment-requests. Sector templates share one rule engine and differ only in thresholds and SKUs:
- food: production lock
- printing: paper and material purchase lock
- florist: stem purchase lock
- events: rental lock
- uniforms and batik: fabric purchase lock
ideas.scope_check:
Not HR or admin: it handles customer orders, deposits and supplier payment requests. Nothing overlaps eLeave, eClaim, eOT, Attendance or Hiring.
No real payments: a deposit is a screenshot or read-only status, and 'Pay supplier' is a request record, with the transfer done by a person in their own bank.
No statutory filing.
Not legal or financial advice: flags say 'unverified, check before you proceed', never 'scam' or 'forged'. The product points to official channels only: the agency's official number, ePerolehan, Semak Mule, and NSRC 997.
PDPA handling:
- buyer names and phone numbers are collected only to fulfil the order, with a notice line on the order form
- the kitchen role cannot see contacts
- personal fields are purged a set period after the order closes (default 12 months); anonymised rule statistics are kept
- role-based access, encryption at rest, and a view log
- no suspected-scammer data is shared between SMEs
The demo uses synthetic data and fictional agencies only.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope:
Build the hold-and-release gate end to end on one scenario:
1. A simulated WhatsApp webhook posts the fake 'PPD Bandar Mutiara' order.
2. It becomes an order card.
3. R2, R3, R4 and R6 fire, and the order goes to HELD with plain reasons.
4. The owner opens the approval screen and records the callback.
5. The owner rejects the order and the log entry appears.
Second beat: the RM9,000 kurma request is blocked by the two-key rule and the cooling-off timer. Contrast: one green consumer order goes straight to the kitchen board.
Seed data: 25 synthetic orders across 3 sectors as JSON, plus a role switcher.
Stack: Next.js plus SQLite or Postgres, with rules as plain, unit-tested functions. Skip the real WhatsApp integration.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback:
Hardest risk: the money is lost in a bank app the product cannot touch, so a pressured owner can bypass the gate.
Mitigation:
- make the gate the only door to production: the kitchen board and ingredient list come only from released orders, so bypassing costs effort
- give daily value (order book, deposit tracking, today's production list) so the tool stays open every day
- the second key sits outside the conversation
- the 24h cooling-off buys time for the pressure to fade
Fallback: if owners will not nominate a second approver, a 'trusted contact' is notified (not asked to approve) of every blocked supplier payment.
Second risk: false positives annoy owners on genuine government orders. Removing the deposit rule for government buyers handles this; one ePerolehan check or official callback clears the order.
Demo risk: WhatsApp API access. A simulated webhook replaces it.
ideas.business_model:
Usage-based on the Orbyte credit wallet:
- Free: up to about 30 orders a month with core rules. For reference, Take App's free plan covers 50 orders a month (vendor claim).
- Transaction: 1 credit per gated order above the threshold.
- Premium: sector templates, multiple outlets, second-approver guest seats.
- Partner: banks and payment partners (fraud-loss reduction, deposit-collection referrals), plus SME and trade associations or state anti-scam campaigns that sponsor seats for members.
Orbyte publishes no RM prices, so any ringgit price we show is our assumption.

ideas.name: LO Lens: AI reader for government and bulk order bundles
ideas.one_liner: Staff forward the WhatsApp chat and the LO (PDF or photo) into Orbyte. AI turns them into a structured order record and highlights every claim that does not match official sources or the shop's own catalogue. The order cannot be accepted, and no linked supplier can be paid, until a person verifies it through ePerolehan or the agency's official number.
ideas.target_user:
Small suppliers that sell to government agencies, schools and companies, and receive orders as WhatsApp messages plus LO documents: printing and stationery shops, souvenir, door-gift and corporate-gift traders, caterers, batik and uniform makers, small IT and equipment resellers. Evidence:
- Raub printing business: RM315,963 lost to a fake PPD LO (The Vibes, 13 Sep 2026)
- Kuantan: five traders, RM89,300, forged LO and vendor appointment letters (The Vibes, 25 Sep 2025)
- Terengganu batik trader: RM48,300 after a WhatsApp 'DOE' order (The Vibes, 10 Mar 2026)
- KL DOE: 8 fake procurement cases, two suppliers losing more than RM200,000 (The Star, 12 Sep 2026)
- KBS impersonation: RM175,452.80 (The Vibes, 15 Jun 2025)
Firm size is not stated in most of these reports, so the targets are small firms and government vendors as well as micro firms.
ideas.trigger:
An institutional or bulk order arrives. In the MVP, staff forward the chat (WhatsApp 'Export chat' text or screenshots) plus the LO file to the shop's Orbyte intake, by simulated webhook or upload.
Automatic rules:
- an inbound attachment named LO, PO or 'Pesanan Tempatan', or a message naming a government agency, opens an intake record
- a new supplier named inside an open bundle triggers a re-check

Synthetic example. A bundle reaches 'Kedai Cetak Seri Mutiara' (fictional, Temerloh, 3 staff): 'Salam tuan, saya Pn. Rosnah, Unit Perolehan PPD Bandar Mutiara (fictional). Kami nak order 200 set fail program + 40 unit projektor utk program minggu depan. LO saya attach. Projektor tu tuan boleh ambil dari pembekal panel kami, Visi Tekno Enterprise, dia akan contact tuan. Urgent ya.' The attached LO.jpg has a letterhead, LO no. PT/BM/2026/0915, contact 011-2345 6789, email ppdbm.perolehan@gmail.com, and a total of RM96,400.
Chinese variant for a gift shop: '你好, 我是XX局采购组, 要订150份door gift, 另外要150盒燕窝, 你们没有的话我介绍供应商给你, 先付一半就可以.'
Genuine control: an email from the synthetic official domain with an LO for 500 printed certificates only.
ideas.connected_data:
- The bundle itself: chat text and the LO image or PDF.
- Shop catalogue, from a POS/e-commerce connector.
- Orbyte clients & projects: has this agency or officer ordered before with a verified LO?
- Approved suppliers and payee names, from the accounting connector.
- Official Agency Directory, curated by Orbyte. Synthetic in the demo; in production built from agencies' own websites. Holds agency name, official landline, official email domain, and whether the agency states it buys only through ePerolehan. KPWKM (The Star, 5 Aug 2026) and MOT (The Star, 2 Oct 2026) both say procurement goes through ePerolehan.
- MO pattern library: short descriptions of police- and media-reported tactics:
  - out-of-catalogue extra items (Perak)
  - buyer-named 'panel' supplier (KBS, Batik, Perak)
  - prepayment to that supplier
  - pay-to-confirm (KPWKM)
  - a PDF LO sent to 'cop dan tandatangan', and requests for company documents 'untuk buat e-Perolehan' (SAYS, 15 Jan 2025)
ideas.decision_logic:
Three layers.
1) AI extraction to a fixed JSON schema: agency, unit, officer, phone numbers, emails, LO number and date, line items (quantity, unit price), total, delivery place, any third party named, any payment instruction. Every field keeps a pointer to its source (chat line or LO region) and a confidence score.
2) Bounded AI judgements:
- Item fit: each line is in catalogue, adjacent, or 'not something we sell'.
- MO match: which library patterns the bundle matches, quoting the exact sentence. For example, 'Projektor tu tuan boleh ambil dari pembekal panel kami' matches the buyer-named supplier pattern.
3) Deterministic rules on top. Each item below is RED:
- a phone number or email not in the directory for that agency
- a mobile number or free email domain on an LO
- a buyer-named supplier
- any request to pay to confirm or register
- a payee-name mismatch
A first-time institutional buyer above the RM threshold triggers 'verification REQUIRED' whatever the AI says.
Principle: AI can add reasons and raise the level. Only a recorded human verification can lower it.

The output is a Verification Plan:
(a) check the LO number in your own ePerolehan account if you are registered
(b) call the directory number, never the number in the message, using a generated BM or English call script that cites the LO number and date
(c) run a Semak Mule check on any payee account or company
If the agency is not in the directory, or a field is unreadable, the plan hands off to a person: 'We could not confirm this agency's official number. Find it on the agency's own website, not in the message.'
ideas.where_ai_adds_value:
AI works at step 2 (pulling connected data out of the bundle) and part of step 3, and nowhere else.
(a) Reading skewed LO photos and PDFs in many layouts, plus WhatsApp chats that code-switch between BM, English, Manglish and Chinese. Templates and regex break on these.
(b) Matching items across languages and synonyms: 'fail program', 'folder' and '文件夹'; 'kurma', 'dates' and '椰枣'. A hand-written alias list is never complete for a newly onboarded SME.
(c) Recognising the tactic when scammers paraphrase it: 'pembekal panel kami', 'supplier yang kami biasa guna', '我介绍供应商给你'. Keyword rules miss rephrased scripts.
What AI does not do:
- decide acceptance
- judge whether a letterhead looks genuine (Miri police warn letterheads can be forged, so visual authenticity is not a reliable test)
- lower any requirement set by the rules
This is the same 'AI reads the document, policy flags it, a human approves' pattern as Orbyte's live eClaim, pointed at money coming in instead of claims going out.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: No one chats with it. A bundle goes in; a structured order record, a verification task list, an approval gate and a log entry come out. The AI is a parsing and classification component with a JSON schema and source pointers, and every flag links back to the exact chat line or LO region. Turn the AI off and you have a manual form running the same rules, not a broken conversation. What judges see is that an order cannot reach Accepted until a named person has recorded verification through an official channel.
ideas.human_approval:
Accepting the order. The owner approves 'Accept order and commit stock or materials' for institutional orders above the threshold, and only after a verification is recorded. Staff cannot accept these orders. The decision screen shows:
- the LO image with extracted fields highlighted, beside the structured record
- the mismatch list, for example 'Phone 011-2345 6789 on the LO is a mobile number; the directory lists an office landline for PPD Bandar Mutiara' and 'Email is gmail.com; the directory domain is the official one'
- an item-fit table ('projektor: not something we sell')
- MO matches with quoted sentences
- the verification record: ePerolehan result, who called which directory number and when, officer name, the answer given
- fields the AI could not read, marked for a person to fill

Supplier payments. Any payment request tied to the bundle (for example a 50% advance of RM46,000 to 'Visi Tekno Enterprise') needs the owner plus a second approver, and is shown with the Semak Mule result and the payee-name check. It is a request record only.

The owner can reject with a reason, or mark the order 'verified genuine'. A verified-genuine order adds the agency, officer and LO to client history, so repeat orders from that buyer go faster.
ideas.roles_and_permissions:
Simulated RBAC.
- Owner: full access. Accepts, rejects or overrides with a typed reason; manages catalogue and thresholds.
- Sales/admin staff: submit bundles, correct extracted fields (every correction is logged with before and after), run verification calls and record results. Cannot accept above the threshold or approve payments.
- Second approver (partner or bookkeeper, guest): sees linked supplier payment requests and their evidence; co-approves. No other access.
- Accounts viewer: sees verified orders only, for delivery orders and invoicing. No raw chats.
- AI service account: reads the submitted bundle only and writes extraction and flags. Cannot change any status.
- Orbyte directory curator (platform role): maintains the official agency directory. No access to tenant data.
ideas.outcome_and_log:
What the user sees: a Verification card. Its status moves from 'UNVERIFIED, 5 reasons' to either 'VERIFIED by Owner via official call, 10:42' or 'REJECTED, agency confirms no such order'. Verified orders flow into a B2G order tracker showing LO number, delivery date, invoice-ready status, and payment expected after delivery. That tracker lines up with Orbyte's stated 'follow up unpaid invoices' direction.

In the example:
- The AI extracts the fields and flags a mobile number and gmail address against the directory, a projector outside the catalogue, a buyer-named supplier, and urgency.
- The owner calls the official PPD landline from the directory and is told there is no such LO.
- The owner rejects the order, and no supplier request is ever created.

The activity log is append-only. It records:
- the bundle received, with its hash
- AI model version and prompt version
- each extracted field with its confidence, plus any human correction (who, before, after)
- each flag with its source pointer
- each verification step: channel, number used and where it came from, outcome
- approvals and rejections with reasons, payment-request keys, exports
It exports as a PDF evidence pack. MOT's statement (The Star, 2 Oct 2026) tells victims to lodge a police report and keep all documents and communication records.
ideas.measurable_benefit:
All figures here are estimates. Averages are our own arithmetic on reported totals.
B2G-style incidents are large:
- Raub: RM315,963
- KBS case: RM175,452.80
- Terengganu batik: RM48,300
- KL DOE: more than RM200,000 across two suppliers
- Kuantan: about RM17,900 per trader (RM89,300 / 5)
Estimate: each prevented incident keeps RM20,000-RM300,000.
Measurable in the demo and a pilot:
- field-level extraction accuracy on the synthetic test set (target 90% or better)
- tactic-detection hit rate on 20 synthetic scam bundles, and false alarms on 20 genuine ones (we report both)
- 100% of first-time institutional orders above the threshold have an official-channel verification recorded before acceptance
- time to turn a bundle into a ready order record instead of retyping the LO (target under 2 minutes; estimate)
Context only: 241 cases and more than RM8 million in 2025, and 80 cases and RM1.9 million to 6 May 2026 (NST/CCID). That figure does not state victim type. Any one business is hit rarely, so the pitch is daily intake value for B2G sellers, with verification working like insurance.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse:
It mirrors Orbyte's live eClaim (AI receipt reading, policy flags, approval) and turns that pattern outward to inbound orders.
Reuses existing Orbyte pieces:
- clients & projects (agency = client, verified LO = project)
- review and approval with audit trail, roles
- optional eSign for delivery acknowledgement
Connect usage:
- accounting: supplier list; approved order and invoice written back to the system of record
- POS and e-commerce: catalogue
- payments: read-only
It fits the stated Business Graph (projects, invoices, payment terms, cash flow).
Reusable building blocks:
(1) Order Bundle Parser API: POST /bundles returns structured order JSON with source pointers, usable by any Orbyte module or partner.
(2) A shared Official Agency Directory, maintained once by Orbyte for all tenants.
(3) An MO pattern library, updated centrally as police publish new tactics.
(4) Sector catalogue templates.
Printers, caterers, gift shops, uniform makers and IT resellers all use it; only the catalogue changes.
ideas.scope_check:
Not HR or admin. No payments processed and no statutory filing. It submits nothing to ePerolehan and does not integrate with any government system; users check their own account.
Not legal advice: it never says 'forged' or 'scam'. It says 'unverified', lists the mismatches, and points to official channels only: the agency's official number, ePerolehan, Semak Mule, and NSRC 997.
PDPA handling:
- Bundles contain third parties' personal data (names, phone numbers). The purpose is verifying an order the business is about to enter.
- Minimise: phone numbers, account numbers and emails are pulled out by local deterministic regex and masked before any text reaches the LLM. Directory matching on those values runs locally.
- The LLM provider is used under no-training, limited-retention terms. Cross-border transfer is handled under PDPA s.129, or avoided with in-region hosting.
- Raw bundles are deleted after 90 days unless the owner places a hold for a police report. The extracted record stays with the order.
- Role-based access and a view audit.
- The directory holds only public office contacts. The MO library holds tactics, not scammer identities. No private blacklist is shared between SMEs.
The demo uses fictional agencies and people only.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope:
One feature: bundle in, verification card out, gate holds. Live demo:
1. Upload the fictional PPD Bandar Mutiara chat and LO image.
2. A vision LLM extracts the fields to the schema, with source highlights.
3. The card shows the directory mismatch, item fit and MO matches.
4. A call script is generated.
5. The owner records the callback outcome.
6. The owner rejects or accepts, and the log entry appears.
Show one genuine bundle passing for contrast.
Seed data: a directory JSON of 10 fictional agencies, 3 catalogues, and 15 bundles (8 scam patterns, 7 genuine) in BM, English and Chinese.
Keep the rule layer deterministic, so the gate still works if the AI is switched off.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback:
Hardest risk: the AI misreads or misses something, and the owner trusts a clean-looking card. Scammers also adapt, for example with landlines or look-alike domains.
Mitigation and fallback:
- AI can never lower the bar: first-time institutional orders above the threshold always need official-channel verification, whatever the AI says.
- Low-confidence fields are left blank for staff to fill.
- If extraction fails entirely, a manual 6-field form runs the same rules.
Directory coverage: if the agency is missing, the hand-off message tells the owner to find the number on the agency's own website.
False positives (genuine officers who use mobiles): the outcome is 'verify', never 'reject', so a genuine buyer costs one call.
Demo risk: LLM latency or outage. Pre-computed results for the seeded bundles plus the deterministic fallback cover it.
ideas.business_model:
Transaction model on the Orbyte credit wallet:
- the first 5 bundle checks a month free, then credits per bundle, which cover AI cost
- Premium for B2G sellers: an order tracker from LO to invoice, with payment-after-delivery follow-up
- Partner: banks and payment providers that want fewer mule-account losses, SME and trade associations, and insurers offering business fraud cover, any of which could subsidise it
Moat: the directory and MO library are maintained once and get better for every tenant.
Orbyte publishes no RM prices, so any ringgit figure we show is our assumption.

ideas.name: Kutip: Cash-Gap Collections Planner
ideas.one_liner: Every morning Kutip checks which bills fall due soon (payroll, rent, supplier) and ranks overdue customer invoices by how much of that cash gap each can close before the date. It prepares tiered WhatsApp reminders in each customer's language. Gentle nudges go out with a clerk's tap, firm ones need the owner's approval, and every step is logged. Kutip is fully rule-based, with no AI.
ideas.target_user: Micro firms (2-10 staff) where the owner or one admin issues invoices from a spreadsheet, a basic invoicing app or a paper book. They sell to business customers on 30-90 day terms and the owner chases payment personally on WhatsApp. Typical sectors are printing and packaging, food and catering supply, wholesale/trading, B2B services and small transport operators. The product is aimed at firms NOT already using Bukku Grow (RM65/month, automatic reminders by email only, per bukku.my fetched 25 Oct 2026) or Xero's automatic reminders. Samenta (FMT, 7 Oct 2025) says 'nearly 30% of SMEs still operate manually'. Two limits apply. Allianz Trade reports an average DSO of 35 days and says delays are 'rare, although likely if the transaction is not secured', so the real target is the subset selling on unsecured credit. No source gives the share of micro firms that sell on credit.
ideas.trigger: There are three triggers. (1) A scheduled scan at 08:00 every working day. (2) An invoice crosses a tier boundary: due date minus 3 days, due date plus 1, plus 14 and plus 30. (3) A known cash outflow (payroll, EPF, rent, supplier bill or loan instalment, entered once as recurring) comes within 14 days and forecast cash falls short. SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE: CetakPantas Print Enterprise (fictional sole proprietorship in Seri Kembangan, 4 staff, prints cake boxes and menus). On Tue 20 Oct 2026 at 08:00 the scan finds salaries plus EPF/SOCSO of RM8,400 due 31 Oct and a paper supplier bill of RM6,800 due 5 Nov. The owner-entered bank balance is RM4,300, and customers who usually pay on time are expected to send RM2,100 before 31 Oct. Kutip shows 'Short RM2,000 for payroll on 31 Oct; short RM8,800 by the supplier bill on 5 Nov' and opens today's chase plan.
ideas.connected_data: (a) Open invoices: number, customer, amount, issue and due date, terms. Sources are an Orbyte Connect accounting connector where one exists, otherwise a CSV or Google Sheet import or manual entry. (b) Customer profile from Orbyte's existing clients records: contact person, WhatsApp number, preferred language (BM/EN/中文), quiet hours, notes such as 'pays via HQ, cheque run on 25th'. (c) Reminder and reply history per invoice. (d) Payment history per customer, from which Kutip computes each customer's own usual 'days to pay after reminder tier X'. (e) Upcoming outflows: payroll date and total (read-only from a payroll/accounting connector, or typed in by the owner), rent, supplier bills, loan instalments. (f) Bank balance, entered by the owner or read from a payments/banking connector later. Synthetic overdue book for CetakPantas: Hock Lee Catering Sdn Bhd INV-0398 RM4,750, due 9 Sep, 41 days overdue, 2 reminders unanswered. Kafe Dua Beradik Sdn Bhd INV-0412 RM3,180, due 2 Oct, 18 days overdue, history shows payment about 4 days after a first nudge. Restoran Selera Kampung INV-0420 RM860, due 15 Oct, 5 days overdue. Tadika Bintang Kecil INV-0405 RM1,240, 21 days overdue, customer promised to pay on 30 Oct.
ideas.decision_logic: Fully deterministic. Every decision shows the rule ID that produced it. R1 Tier: D-3 courtesy, D+1 nudge, D+14 firm with statement attached, D+30 or a Tier 2 unanswered for 7 days becomes an owner-only escalation card with no automatic message. R2 Suppression: skip if the invoice is marked disputed, a promised date has not yet passed, a payment was logged in the last 2 days, it is quiet hours (default before 9am or after 8pm), or the customer was messaged in the last 5 days. R3 Priority: rank invoices by expected cash before the next shortfall date = amount x the customer's historical rate of paying within N days at this tier (default 50% for new customers). Then pick the smallest set that covers the gap. R4 Credit hold: a new order on credit from a customer with an invoice more than 30 days overdue raises an owner card ('Accept on credit / Ask for COD / Call first'). R5 Language and template come from the customer profile. Fixed templates per tier per language use only merge fields. CetakPantas result on 20 Oct: #1 Kafe Dua Beradik Tier 1 (likely to pay before 31 Oct and covers the RM2,000 payroll gap). #2 Hock Lee Catering Tier 2 (needed for 5 Nov, so owner approval is required). #3 Restoran Selera Kampung Tier 1. Tadika Bintang Kecil is skipped with the reason 'R2: promise 30 Oct not reached'. Sample messages: Tier 1 Manglish: 'Hi Encik Faizal, Mei Ling from CetakPantas here. Friendly reminder ya, INV-0412 for the 500 cake boxes (RM3,180) was due 2 Oct. Can help check with your accounts? Statement attached. Thank you!' Tier 1 BM: 'Assalamualaikum Puan Rosnah, ini Mei Ling dari CetakPantas. Peringatan mesra, invois INV-0420 (RM860) untuk menu bercetak telah tamat tempoh pada 15 Okt. Mohon semak ya. Terima kasih!' Tier 2 Chinese: '李老板您好，我是CetakPantas的美玲。INV-0398（RM4,750）已经逾期41天，之前提醒了两次。麻烦在10月30日前安排付款，或回复告诉我们付款日期。附上对账单，谢谢！'
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: AI is not needed, and the pitch should say so on purpose. Tiers, suppression, ranking against a dated cash gap and credit holds are plain arithmetic and date rules on structured data. Rules make every outcome explainable in one line ('R3: closes 100% of the 31 Oct payroll gap; this customer usually pays 4 days after a nudge'), testable and cheap, which is what an owner who must approve a firm message to a long-standing customer needs. That answers the rubric's 'AI only where it adds value'. Reading customers' free-text replies is the job where AI does help, and that belongs to the second concept (Bukti), which can plug into Kutip later.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no conversation anywhere. Kutip is a scheduled engine that turns an invoice ledger and a list of upcoming outflows into a ranked chase plan, a cash-gap meter and an approval queue. Outbound text comes from fixed, owner-approved templates, not generated prose. Judges see ledger state changing, a gap closing and an audit log, not a chat window.
ideas.human_approval: Owner: approves every Tier 2 (firm) message, every Tier 3 escalation choice (call / stop credit / refer to the firm's own lawyer, with no legal text generated), every credit-hold decision and any template change. Admin/clerk: may approve Tier 0/1 courtesy and nudge messages. After a 2-week trial the owner can switch Tier 0/1 to auto-send per customer, and can switch it off at any time. What the approver sees on each card: customer, invoice, amount, days overdue, past reminders and any replies, the customer's payment pattern, the exact message preview in the customer's language, the rule that fired, and the gap impact (for example 'If paid by 30 Oct: 5 Nov shortfall drops RM8,800 to RM4,050'). Buttons: Approve & send, Edit text, Snooze to date, Mark disputed, I'll call instead.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated RBAC on Orbyte's existing role and approval framework. OWNER: sees everything, including bank balance, payroll total and cash gap. Approves Tier 2/3 and credit holds, edits templates and terms. ADMIN/CLERK: imports invoices, records payments received, approves Tier 0/1, sees the aging list. Cannot see the payroll amount or bank balance (only 'gap: yes/no'), cannot send Tier 2/3 and cannot change credit status. SALES REP: read-only status for their own customers (paid / overdue / on credit hold), so they do not promise new credit to a blocked customer. No cash figures. EXTERNAL ACCOUNTANT: read-only export of the aging report and activity log.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees: (1) a cash-gap meter per upcoming outflow ('31 Oct payroll: short RM2,000, now covered by promised RM3,180') that updates as payments are logged; (2) each invoice's timeline (reminders, replies, promises, payment); (3) a 'no next action' counter that should stay at zero. Activity log (append-only, with timestamp, actor and rule ID). Example: '20 Oct 08:00 SYSTEM scan: 9 open, 4 overdue, payroll gap RM2,000 (31 Oct), supplier gap RM8,800 (5 Nov)'. '08:00 RULE R2 skipped INV-0405: promise 30 Oct not reached'. '08:01 RULE R3 proposed Tier 1 INV-0412 (rank 1), Tier 2 INV-0398 (rank 2)'. '08:47 CLERK Aisyah approved Tier 1 INV-0412, sent via WhatsApp'. '09:15 OWNER Tan Mei Ling approved Tier 2 INV-0398 (edited pay-by date 31 Oct to 30 Oct), sent'. '23 Oct 14:40 CLERK Aisyah recorded RM3,180 received for INV-0412; payroll gap now covered'. The log is exportable as CSV for the accountant.
ideas.measurable_benefit: ALL FIGURES BELOW ARE ESTIMATES TO BE VALIDATED WITH SME OWNERS. Cash released, by arithmetic: CetakPantas sells about RM45,000/month on credit (synthetic), so each day cut from collection time frees about RM1,500 once. If prioritised, consistent chasing shortens collection on chased invoices by 5-7 days (an assumption: the verifier found no Malaysian source showing reminders shorten collection time), that frees about RM7,500-10,500 once. That would cover the illustrated payroll gap without an overdraft or late supplier payment. Process metrics measurable from day one: overdue invoices with no next action (target 0); days from due date to first reminder (target D+1, against the ad-hoc chasing owners describe on Lowyat, 2021: 'Always 30 days became 60/90/120 days'); shortfall warnings at least 10 days before payroll. Owner chasing time is NOT quantified in any source, so it will be measured in validation interviews, not claimed. Context, quoted with caveats: Experian (21 May 2025) reports SME 'payment delays' averaging 64 days against 58 for large corporates, without defining whether SMEs are the payer or the payee. BNM's Assistant Governor (The Star, 30 Jul 2026) names 'slower customer payments' as one of three drivers of working-capital need. Samenta (FMT, 7 Oct 2025): '70% of SMEs had less than six months' worth of cash reserves'. SDG 8.3: protects MSME cash flow. SDG 8.2: owner time moves from chasing to selling.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: Kutip delivers the receivables item already on Orbyte's stated roadmap ('follow up unpaid invoices') and feeds the planned Business Graph that links invoices, payment terms and cash flow. It reuses Orbyte's existing platform pieces: clients records as the customer master, roles, the review-and-approval engine and the audit trail. Data comes through Orbyte Connect categories (accounting for invoices and payroll totals, payments and collections for settlements). Approved results are written back to the system of record, as Orbyte already does. It does NOT touch Orbyte's People modules beyond reading a payroll date and total as a cash outflow. Reuse across SMEs: a sector-agnostic 'Receivables Follow-up' module with config packs (tier schedule, terms, BM/EN/中文 templates, quiet hours, sector fields such as DO number for transport, job number for printing, event date for catering). It also exposes a small API: POST /receivables/invoices, GET /receivables/chase-plan?date=, POST /receivables/approvals, and webhooks invoice.overdue, chase.approved, gap.detected. Other Orbyte modules or partners can subscribe to these.
ideas.scope_check: NOT HR/admin: this is receivables, in the finance/sales domain, and Orbyte has no live module for it. No real payments: Kutip moves no money, any pay link in the demo is simulated, and payments are recorded from the owner's own bank. No statutory filing: no e-invoice or tax submission. No legal or financial advice: there are no letters of demand and no legal wording. Tier 3 is a hand-off card to the owner, and 'refer to own lawyer' is a choice the owner makes, not advice. Late-interest wording is not generated, because in Malaysia interest must be contractual (Allianz Trade). The cash gap is arithmetic on figures the owner enters, not a lending recommendation. PDPA: the demo uses synthetic customers and fictional numbers only. In production, a customer contact person's name and phone number are personal data under PDPA 2010 (as amended in 2024). The SME is the data user and Orbyte/Kutip acts as its processor. Principles applied: purpose limitation (used only to follow up invoices the customer already received), a notice line on invoices, role-based access (clerk and sales cannot see cash figures), opt-out honoured per contact, retention limit after the account closes, data encrypted at rest, and breach-notification readiness under the 2024 amendments.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: Build the 'Morning Chase Plan' journey end to end on synthetic data: (1) load a CSV of about 15 CetakPantas invoices plus 3 outflows; (2) press 'Run 08:00 scan' to show the cash-gap meter and a ranked list with a rule reason on each row and one visibly skipped invoice; (3) log in as Owner (simulated role switch) and approve the Tier 2 Chinese message to Hock Lee Catering from its preview card; (4) the send is simulated, or a wa.me link opens real WhatsApp with the text prefilled; (5) switch to Clerk, record the RM3,180 payment from Kafe Dua Beradik, then watch the gap meter update and the activity log show every step with actor and rule ID. Credit hold, Tier 0 auto-send and connectors are roadmap slides.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: Risk 1, demand risk (the biggest one): the verifier found no evidence that reminders shorten collection. Many slow payers are corporates, GLCs or government bodies paying on their own cycles; Minister Wee (2017) said SMEs 'lacked the voice to demand' payment. Mitigation: the pitch rests on prioritisation against dated outflows, the credit-hold rule (stop extending credit to customers already 30+ days late) and visibility, not on 'automated reminders', which Bukku and Xero already sell. Validate with 3-5 owners before the final round, asking how many hours a week they chase and whether they would let a clerk send nudges. Risk 2, the WhatsApp channel: business-initiated messages on the official WhatsApp Business Platform need Meta business verification, pre-approved templates and per-message fees. Fallback: wa.me click-to-send (prefilled text opens the owner's own WhatsApp and the owner presses send), which needs no API approval and strengthens human control. The demo simulates the send. Risk 3, data entry burden for firms with no software: fallback is CSV/Sheet import plus a 20-second manual invoice form. Photo-of-invoice capture is roadmap.
ideas.business_model: Fits Orbyte's credit wallet and per-unit charging (Orbyte publishes no RM prices, so the figures here are illustrative only). Free: up to 10 open invoices tracked with manual reminders. Usage: a small credit charge per invoice actively chased per month, and per WhatsApp send when the official API is used (passing on Meta's per-message cost). Target: a typical micro firm should pay less than Bukku Grow's RM65/month, with WhatsApp delivery and owner-approved tiers as the reasons to switch. Premium: multi-entity, more outflow sources, credit-hold enforcement linked to sales or POS connectors. Partner (roadmap): a neutral hand-off to factoring or invoice-financing partners through Orbyte Connect's financing-referral category, only when the owner asks. The product does not recommend a lender. FocusM (28 Oct 2025) describes factoring in Malaysia as 'under-utilised'. Growth path: start with printing, packaging and catering suppliers, then transport and wholesale; Kutip later consumes Bukti's parsed replies.

ideas.name: Bukti: WhatsApp Payment-Proof & Promise Reconciler
ideas.one_liner: Bukti reads the transfer-slip screenshots and messy Manglish, BM and Chinese replies customers send on WhatsApp ('dah bank in boss', 'bayar separuh dulu', '下礼拜五才过数'). It extracts the amount, reference, promised date and any deduction reason, and checks the payment against the bank statement. It matches the payment to open invoices, flags short-payments and disputes, and turns each message into a one-tap approval that keeps the ledger correct, so paid customers are never chased and promises and deductions never slip through.
ideas.target_user: Small firms (roughly 8-30 staff) with high invoice volume and a dedicated account clerk who reconciles collections by hand from WhatsApp chats, a bank app and a spreadsheet. Best fit: transport and logistics (per-trip invoices; Experian, 21 May 2025, puts transport/logistics at 76 days on average and the widest SME-corporate gap, 26 days in 1Q 2025), wholesale/trading, food and catering distributors, and building-material suppliers. Micro firms benefit too, but the time saving scales with the number of slips.
ideas.trigger: An inbound customer message or image arrives in the business's collections WhatsApp number (official WhatsApp Business Platform webhook in production). Alternatives are the clerk forwarding or sharing a slip into Bukti, or a daily bank-statement CSV import that triggers matching of unclaimed credits. SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE: Lori Laju Logistics Sdn Bhd (fictional, Klang, 14 staff, lorry haulage). On Tue 27 Oct 2026 at 10:14, Jessie, the account clerk at customer Mega Bina Hardware Trading (fictional), sends: 'Hi kak, payment for Sept trips done already ya, I bank in RM7,420 just now. Got deduct RM330 for the 2 pallet tiles pecah at Bukit Raja. Slip attached'. She attaches a transfer screenshot from a fictional bank showing RM7,420.00 with reference 'LLL SEPT'. The same morning two more messages arrive. Restoran Nasi Kandar Pelita Jaya (fictional): 'Encik, bulan ni kami bayar separuh dulu RM2,000, baki hujung bulan depan ok?' Syarikat Hup Seng Trading (fictional): '老板，那张发票我们下礼拜五才可以过数，sorry ah'.
ideas.connected_data: (a) Open invoices with line references: Mega Bina has INV-2291 RM2,850 (trip 3 Sep, DO-8790), INV-2304 RM3,100 (trip 12 Sep, DO-8812, destination Bukit Raja) and INV-2317 RM1,800 (trip 24 Sep, DO-8841), totalling RM7,750. (b) Delivery orders and proof-of-delivery photos from the ops side (driver's signed DO). (c) The bank statement CSV, or later a payments/banking connector feed; the 27 Oct line reads 'DUITNOW CR RM7,420.00 MEGA BINA HARDW LLL SEPT'. (d) A customer contact map (which WhatsApp numbers belong to which customer account). (e) Existing promises, credit notes and the reminder state (from Kutip if installed). (f) Tolerance settings set by the owner, for example auto-propose only when the difference is RM0.00.
ideas.decision_logic: Two layers: AI extracts, rules decide. LAYER 1 (AI) turns each message and image into structured JSON with a confidence score and the quoted source span per field: intent (PAID_CLAIM / PARTIAL / PROMISE_TO_PAY / DISPUTE_OR_DEDUCTION / DOC_REQUEST / OTHER), amount, date, bank reference, deduction amount and reason, and promised date (resolved from relative expressions). LAYER 2 (deterministic rules): M1 a slip counts only as a 'claim'; status becomes VERIFIED only when a bank line with the same amount and a payer-name match exists within 3 days. M2 allocation tries an exact single-invoice match, then the oldest-first exact combination of up to 5 invoices, then flags the difference. M3 a stated deduction is linked to an invoice when its reason text matches the DO destination or item. M4 any field below 0.85 confidence, or any unmatched difference, goes to a human with a specific question. M5 reminders for any invoice in a claim, promise or dispute are paused automatically. Results for the example: Mega Bina: the bank line matches (VERIFIED). INV-2291 and INV-2317 are proposed PAID. INV-2304 is proposed PART-PAID RM2,770 with a RM330 deduction under review, linked through 'Bukit Raja' to DO-8812. Pelita Jaya: PARTIAL + PROMISE; RM2,000 is awaited on the bank feed and the balance RM1,450 is promised for 'hujung bulan depan', resolved to 30 Nov, with a follow-up set for 1 Dec. Hup Seng: PROMISE_TO_PAY, '下礼拜五' resolved to Fri 6 Nov but marked AMBIGUOUS (30 Oct or 6 Nov), so the clerk confirms. If a 'settle already la' claim arrives with no slip and no bank line, Bukti does not mark it paid; it drafts a reply for approval: 'Hi Jessie, thanks! We can't see it in our bank yet, can share the slip or transfer ref? Thank you'.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: AI is used at exactly one step: step 2-3, reading unstructured inbound proof and replies into fields. Rules alone cannot do this for three reasons. (1) Payment slips come as screenshots in many bank and e-wallet layouts, sometimes cropped, forwarded or photographed, so template parsing breaks with each new layout. (2) Replies mix Manglish, BM and Chinese in one sentence, with relative and culturally specific dates ('hujung bulan depan', '下礼拜五', 'after raya') and deduction reasons in free text that must be tied to a specific delivery. (3) The same words carry different intents ('settle already' can be a paid claim or a promise). A vision-capable LLM returns structured JSON with confidence scores and quoted spans. AI does NOT decide anything about money: matching, verification against the bank line, allocation and status changes are deterministic rules, and anything uncertain is handed to a human with a precise question. This mirrors Orbyte's own eClaim pattern (AI receipt reading plus policy flags plus approval), applied to the money-in side.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: Bukti never converses with customers or with the owner. It is an inbox-to-ledger pipeline: messages in, structured extraction, rule-based matching against invoices and bank lines, then an approval queue showing an allocation table and a ledger update. The only outbound text is an occasional templated reply that a human approves. The AI is a hidden extraction component; what the judges see is a slip image with highlighted fields next to a proposed allocation table and a short-payment flag.
ideas.human_approval: ACCOUNT CLERK approves routine allocations where the bank line is VERIFIED and the difference is RM0, confirms ambiguous promised dates, and approves templated replies asking for a missing slip. OWNER/DIRECTOR approves anything that changes what the customer owes: accepting a deduction (which drafts a credit note for the accounting system), rejecting a deduction (a customer-facing reply with the POD photo attached), writing off a short-payment, or accepting a promised date more than 30 days past the due date. OPS/DISPATCH SUPERVISOR attaches POD evidence to a dispute but cannot approve money changes. The approval card shows the original WhatsApp message and slip image with each extracted field highlighted and its confidence, the matched bank-statement line, the proposed allocation table (invoice, amount due, amount applied, difference), the linked DO and POD photo for any deduction, the rule IDs that fired, and what will be written back. Buttons: Approve, Edit allocation, Ask customer (template), Send to Ops, Reject.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated RBAC on Orbyte roles. OWNER: everything; sets tolerances; only role that can accept or reject deductions, write off, or approve long promise extensions. ACCOUNT CLERK: collections inbox, extraction results, bank lines, allocation approvals at zero difference, promise calendar, templated replies; cannot create credit notes or write-offs. OPS/DISPATCH SUPERVISOR: sees only disputes linked to their deliveries plus DO/POD; uploads evidence; cannot see bank lines or other customers' balances. SALES/ACCOUNT MANAGER: read-only customer status, open promises and disputes for their accounts. EXTERNAL ACCOUNTANT: read-only export of allocations, credit-note drafts and the log.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees: the customer ledger updated (INV-2291 PAID, INV-2317 PAID, INV-2304 PART-PAID RM2,770 with deduction RM330 under review), reminders paused on those invoices, and a promise calendar (Hup Seng 6 Nov, Pelita Jaya balance RM1,450 on 30 Nov). A daily strip reads 'Verified cash in today RM7,420 / Open short-payments RM330 / Promises due this week 1'. Activity log (append-only, with actor, timestamp, rule ID and confidence). Example: '27 Oct 10:14 INBOUND Mega Bina (Jessie) text + image'. '10:14 AI extract amount 7,420.00 (0.98), ref LLL SEPT (0.95), deduction 330.00 reason "2 pallet tiles pecah at Bukit Raja" (0.88)'. '10:15 RULE M1 VERIFIED vs bank line 27/10 DUITNOW CR 7,420.00'. '10:15 RULE M2/M3 proposal: 2291 full, 2317 full, 2304 2,770 + deduction 330 linked DO-8812'. '10:31 CLERK Nurul approved 2291 and 2317'. '11:05 OPS Ravi attached POD-8812 (handover note: 2 pallets damaged)'. '11:20 OWNER Lim accepted RM330 deduction; credit note CN-0057 drafted for the accounting system (not submitted)'. '11:22 Written back to accounting system of record (simulated)'.
ideas.measurable_benefit: ALL FIGURES BELOW ARE ESTIMATES OR ASSUMPTIONS TO VALIDATE; NO SOURCE QUANTIFIES THEM. Clerk time: assume Lori Laju receives about 120 payment messages or slips a month and manual matching takes about 6 minutes each (find invoices, check the bank app, update the sheet), about 12 hours a month. Review-only at about 1 minute each would be about 2 hours, saving about 10 clerk-hours a month. Money surfaced: if 1-2% of about RM150,000 monthly collections arrive with unexplained or unagreed deductions (assumption), RM1,500-3,000 a month gets an explicit owner decision instead of being found at year-end or never. Promise slippage: every promise gets a follow-up the day after it falls due, measured as promise-kept rate and days from promise to cash. Wrongful chasing of customers who have already paid falls to zero, because reminders pause on any claim. Accuracy, measurable now: a synthetic test set of 50 slips (fictional bank layouts) and 50 code-mixed messages, reporting field-level accuracy (target: at least 95% on amount), plus zero invoices marked PAID without a matching bank line by design. Context: Experian (21 May 2025) puts transport/logistics at 76 days average payment delay, with the payer/payee direction undefined. Funding Societies' regional survey (2023, not Malaysia-specific) says manual reminders lead to neglected follow-ups. SDG 8.2 (clerk productivity) and 8.3 (MSME cash protection); SDG 9 (digital infrastructure for small firms).
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: Bukti extends a pattern Orbyte already ships, AI document reading plus policy flags plus approval (eClaim), to customer payments, a domain Orbyte has not built. It is not a copy: eClaim handles employee expense reimbursements (HR), while Bukti handles customer receivables (finance/sales). It reuses Orbyte's approval engine, roles, audit trail and clients records. Data comes through Orbyte Connect's payments and collections connectors (bank and payment feeds) and the accounting connector, which receives approved allocations and credit-note drafts, consistent with Orbyte writing approved results back to the system of record. It populates the Business Graph (payment to invoice to delivery). Reusable building block: a 'Payment Proof API'. POST /proofs (image and/or text, customer hint) returns the extraction JSON plus match proposals; POST /proofs/{id}/decision records an approval; webhooks fire proof.verified, shortpay.detected and promise.due. Sector packs map deduction reasons to sector objects: DO/trip for transport, PO/SKU for wholesale, event date for catering, job number for printing. Language packs: BM, EN, 中文 and code-mixed. It can feed Kutip (concept 1) so chasing pauses automatically on claims and promises.
ideas.scope_check: NOT HR/admin: these are customer receipts in the finance domain, not employee claims. No real payments: Bukti only reads proof of transfers the customer already made and imports a bank statement; it moves no money. No statutory filing: credit notes are drafted for the SME's own accounting system and nothing is submitted to MyInvois or LHDN. No legal or financial advice: deduction disputes are decided by the owner, and Bukti only assembles the evidence (message, slip, DO, POD). Synthetic data: demo slips must use fictional bank names and layouts, not imitations of real Malaysian banks' receipts, to avoid fabricating real-institution records. PDPA: slips contain payer names and partial account numbers, which are personal data under PDPA 2010 (as amended in 2024). Handling: extract only the needed fields, mask account numbers immediately, store the image encrypted with a retention limit (for example the audit period set by the owner), keep bank lines invisible to Ops and Sales, and use an AI provider that does not train on customer data. Cross-border transfer obligations apply if the model is hosted outside Malaysia, so disclose this and prefer in-region hosting. The SME is the data user and Orbyte/Bukti is the processor.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: One slip, end to end. (1) A simulated collections inbox receives Jessie's Manglish message plus a synthetic slip screenshot. (2) A live vision-LLM call shows extracted fields highlighted on the image with confidence scores. (3) The rule matcher checks the synthetic bank CSV line, proposes the 3-invoice allocation, and flags the RM330 short-payment linked to DO-8812. (4) Role switch: Ops attaches the POD photo, then the Owner accepts the deduction. (5) The ledger updates, reminders pause, and the activity log shows every step. If time allows, show the '下礼拜五' ambiguity card as the explainable hand-off moment. Bank feeds, the WhatsApp webhook and the promise calendar are roadmap slides.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: Risk 1, extraction errors marking money as received when it was not. Mitigations: by design a slip never sets PAID without a matching bank line (rule M1); a confidence threshold routes low-confidence fields to a human; amounts are cross-checked between slip, text and bank line. Demo fallback: a cached extraction JSON for the demo slip if the live model call fails or is slow, plus a manual form prefilled with whatever was extracted. Risk 2, getting messages in: the official WhatsApp Business Platform needs business verification. We have not verified whether it can read existing customer group chats, where many slips are posted today, so we assume it cannot. Fallback: customers or the clerk forward slips to the business's collections number, or the clerk uses the share sheet or upload; the demo uses a simulated inbox. Risk 3, scarce real slip data for testing: build a synthetic set with fictional bank layouts, then validate on a few real, anonymised slips from consenting SME owners after the preliminary round.
ideas.business_model: Per-unit credits, matching Orbyte's existing per-claim charging for eClaim: a small credit per proof processed. Exact or verified matches could be cheaper than ones needing review. Orbyte publishes no RM prices, so amounts are left as illustrative. Freemium: the first 30 proofs a month are free, to reach micro firms. Premium: automatic bank-feed matching through payments/banking connectors, multi-number inbox, sector packs. Partner: revenue share with bank and payment-connector partners whose feeds enable VERIFIED matching. Growth path: transport and logistics first (widest payment gap in the Experian data), then wholesale and food distribution. The extraction API can then be offered to other Orbyte modules and to accounting partners as a reusable 'payment proof' service.

ideas.name: VO Catcher: WhatsApp site instructions to signed variation confirmations
ideas.one_liner: Turns the extra-work instructions that main contractors give on WhatsApp (text, photo, voice note, in Manglish, BM or Chinese) into priced variation confirmations. The owner approves each one and the main contractor e-signs it, so the extra work goes into the next progress claim and is not written off.
ideas.target_user: Owners, project managers and in-house QS or admin staff at micro and small B2B subcontractors working under main contractors or developers. Trades include M&E, commercial fit-out, aluminium and glazing, plumbing and fire protection. Homeowner renovation is roadmap only: under CIPAA s.3, contracts with a natural person for a building under four storeys wholly for their own occupation fall outside the Act. Evidence honesty: 48% of CIPAA claimants in 2014-2017 were subcontractors (KLRCA CIPAA Report 2017). No source isolates micro or small firms, so treat the evidence as 'construction SMEs including medium' until interviews confirm it.
ideas.trigger:
EVENT: new site messages reach the project inbox. In the demo, the PM uploads a synthetic WhatsApp 'Export chat' .txt. In production, the PM forwards to an Orbyte project number or uses the share sheet. We do not assume API access to WhatsApp group chats. SCHEDULE: 3 working days before the claim cut-off (the 25th in the example), a sweep lists any instruction still unconfirmed. Synthetic example: Arus Cekap M&E Sdn Bhd (fictional, 9 staff) holds an RM860,000 M&E subcontract on 'Residensi Seri Kenanga Block B' (fictional) under Mega Tiang Builders Sdn Bhd (fictional). Export excerpt:
06/10/2026, 08:14 - Ah Seng (MTB site spv): Faizal, level 3 unit 3-05 sampai 3-08 tambah 2 power point each unit, owner request. Before Friday can ah?
06/10/2026, 08:20 - Faizal (Arus PM): Ok noted boss
09/10/2026, 17:42 - Ah Seng: <photo> DB L3 tukar 63A la, 40A tak cukup. Follow drawing rev C.
13/10/2026, 09:03 - Ah Seng: 走廊的灯先不要装，等ID confirm先
15/10/2026, 07:10 - Ah Seng: <voice note> 'Esok crane datang pukul 7, team you standby ya'
18/10/2026, 14:05 - Ah Seng: Bos minta semua bilik air level 4 & 5 ada water heater point. 24 unit total. Start minggu depan.
20/10/2026, 11:30 - Ah Seng: Cable tray L2 ikut drawing kan? ok good
ideas.connected_data: Orbyte Clients & Projects: the project, the main contractor and its contacts. Subcontract scope and BQ with rates, uploaded once per project as CSV (BQ lines such as E-4.2 '13A twin socket outlet incl. wiring' at RM180 and E-2.1 'DB 40A TPN' at RM1,380). Drawing revision list. Supplier quotes held by QS. VO register history (duplicate check). Month's progress-claim draft. Orbyte eSign (Documenso) envelope status. Accounting system via Orbyte Connect, mocked: confirmed VOs pushed as claim lines. All demo data is synthetic.
ideas.decision_logic: Hybrid. AI first: (1) classify each message as INSTRUCTION-ADD, INSTRUCTION-CHANGE, HOLD, QUESTION/CONFIRMS-SCOPE or COORDINATION. (2) Extract location, item, quantity, deadline, the person giving the instruction and the source message ID. (3) Match the item to BQ lines semantically. Then deterministic rules: (a) BQ rate found: price automatically. (b) No rate: route to QS for a quoted rate. (c) Confidence below 0.8 or an ambiguous quantity: mandatory PM confirmation, with the ambiguity spelt out. (d) Same item and location within 14 days: merge as a duplicate. (e) Value at or above RM2,000 (configurable) needs Owner approval to send; below that, the PM may approve. (f) Sent but unsigned after 5 working days: reminder task. (g) At claim cut-off, split VOs into Confirmed and Pending. Example results: 8 x 13A socket (4 units x 2, quantity flagged for PM) at RM180 = RM1,440. DB swap: omit RM1,380, add 63A at a QS-quoted RM2,150, net +RM770. 24 water heater points at RM260 = RM6,240. Corridor lights become a dated HOLD record with no RM value and no entitlement judgement. The crane message is COORDINATION and is archived only. Cable tray is CONFIRMS-SCOPE: no VO. Month total proposed: RM8,450.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: Step 3, at three jobs rules cannot do reliably. (1) Deciding which of hundreds of site messages is an instruction that changes scope. The same instruction arrives as 'tambah', 'add', 'tukar', '先不要装', a photo caption or a voice note, with code-switching and site slang ('PP', 'plug point', 'soket'). (2) Extracting structured quantity and location from loose phrasing ('3-05 sampai 3-08 ... 2 each unit' means 4 units x 2 = 8), and flagging when phrasing is ambiguous. (3) Matching free-text items to formal BQ descriptions ('power point' to '13A twin socket outlet incl. wiring'). A keyword list misses phrasings and drowns the PM in false hits. AI does NOT price, approve, send or judge entitlement. Rules and humans do those.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: Nobody chats with it. It is an event-driven pipeline: messages in, structured and priced VO records out, an approval gate, an e-signed document and a register entry. The AI is invisible plumbing inside step 3. The deliverables are a signed PDF, a VO register line, a claim line and an audit trail, not a conversation. The demo shows a source WhatsApp bubble next to a priced VO card with highlighted extracted words, which no chatbot reskin produces.
ideas.human_approval: Gate 1, sending a 'Request for Written Confirmation of Site Instruction' to the main contractor's contracts manager through Orbyte eSign. The Owner/Director approves (or the PM, below RM2,000). The approver sees the original message bubble with timestamp, sender and photo. Extracted words are highlighted. They also see the matched BQ line and where the rate came from (BQ or QS quote), any PM edits as a diff, ambiguity and confidence flags, the RM value, and the project's running totals (unconfirmed, sent, signed). Actions: approve, edit, reject as 'not a variation', or mark 'goodwill, no charge'. Gate 2: the Owner approves including Confirmed VOs (and, separately, any Pending ones) in the month's progress-claim draft. The AI can never send anything externally.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated RBAC. OWNER/DIRECTOR: all projects; approves external sends and claim inclusion; sets thresholds; views the full log. PROJECT MANAGER: own projects only; ingests and forwards messages; confirms or edits AI extracts; approves sends below threshold. QS/ADMIN: maintains BQ rates and quotes; prepares the claim draft; cannot approve or send. SITE FOREMAN: forward or upload only; sees own submissions. EXTERNAL MAIN-CONTRACTOR SIGNER: a one-document eSign link, nothing else. EXTERNAL ACCOUNTANT/ADVISER: read-only evidence-pack export, only when the Owner shares it. AI SERVICE ACCOUNT: writes suggestions only; no approve or send rights.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees a per-project VO Register with status chips (Captured, Proposed, Approved, Sent, Signed, Disputed or No-response) and RM totals. Example after one month: Proposed RM8,450, Sent RM8,450, Signed RM6,240 (water heaters), Pending RM2,210. The month's claim draft shows a 'Variations: confirmed / pending' section. Activity log, one line per event, append-only. 2026-10-21 10:02 AI-extract v0.3 created VO-CAND-014 from msg#0412 (hash a3f9...): '13A twin socket, units 3-05..3-08, qty 8', conf 0.78, qty ambiguous. 10:09 Faizal (PM) confirmed qty 8, note 'checked on site'. 10:15 RULE priced it at BQ E-4.2 x RM180 = RM1,440. 11:30 Mei Ling (Owner) approved VO-CR-014..016, total RM8,450. 11:31 eSign ENV-7781 sent to the main contractor's contracts manager (simulated). 2026-10-23 16:40 ENV-7781 partially signed: VO-CR-016 RM6,240 confirmed. Each entry stores the actor (human, or AI with model version), before and after values, source message hash and envelope ID.
ideas.measurable_benefit: ESTIMATES, to validate with 3-5 subcontractor interviews. (1) Primary KPI: RM of instructed extra work with written confirmation before claim cut-off.
