The synthetic month shows RM8,450 on one RM860,000 subcontract (about 1%). That ratio is an assumption, not a sourced figure. (2) Claim-prep time: compiling VOs by scrolling chats, estimated at 3-5 hours per project per month, falls to under 1 hour (estimate). (3) Cost context (sourced): if a payment dispute reaches AIAC adjudication, the adjudicator fee alone is RM3,036 (claims up to RM50,000) or RM6,336 (RM50,001-150,000), excluding taxes. P.U.(A) 364/2025 re-gazetted these amounts, in force 1 Jan 2026. Lawyer costs are extra but no source quantifies them. We do NOT claim the product prevents disputes. No source quantifies how often subcontractors lose disputes for lack of documents, so 'a signed record shortens arguments' is a hypothesis to test.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: Reuses Orbyte Clients & Projects (project = subcontract), eSign on Documenso with audit log (main-contractor signature, and per-signed-document charging already exists), platform approval workflows with audit trail, and the credit wallet. Connect's accounting category (Bukku, SQL or AutoCount, mocked) receives confirmed VOs as claim lines. It adds the WhatsApp channel and customer-facing workflow that Orbyte lacks, and it feeds the stated 'Business Graph' direction (projects, invoices, payment terms). Reusable building block: a 'Change-Request Capture' module and API. Input: a message stream plus a price or scope list. Output: priced change records, then approval, then eSign. The price list is a BQ for construction and a catalogue or rate card elsewhere. The same engine serves signage and printing shops, event vendors, IT and CCTV installers, B2B fabrication workshops and agencies: any SME whose clients change scope on WhatsApp. It chains with HoldBack Ledger (idea 2): confirmed VOs flow into the claim and exposure ledger.
ideas.scope_check: Not HR/admin. Orbyte eClaim handles employee expense claims; this handles B2B revenue from variation works. No real payments. No statutory filing: it never drafts CIPAA s.5 payment claims, adjudication notices or s.29 suspension notices. No legal advice: it does not interpret contract clauses, judge entitlement, or recommend adjudication. The confirmation request uses the firm's own template and states facts only (who instructed what, when, at which BQ rate) for the main contractor to confirm. It is labelled 'not legal advice'. The pitch must not present pay-when-paid as lawful, because CIPAA s.35 voids conditional-payment clauses in covered contracts. PDPA: the demo uses only synthetic chats and names. In production, only messages the user chooses to forward or export for a project are ingested, for the purpose of contract records. Phone numbers are masked before any AI call, and customer data is never used for model training. Access is by role, retention is tied to project close plus the defects period (configurable), and deletion is available on request. Breach handling follows PDPA 2010 as amended in 2024.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: Build live: the extraction-to-approval screen. Upload a synthetic WhatsApp export (about 40 messages in Manglish, BM and Chinese, one project). The left pane shows source bubbles with highlighted spans. The right pane shows AI-proposed VO cards, each with its BQ match, rule-based price, confidence and ambiguity flag. The PM fixes one ambiguous quantity, and the Owner sees the approval card and approves. The app then generates the VO confirmation PDF, updates the register status and writes log lines. Mock eSign as a 'Mark signed' button and the accounting push as JSON. Seed the BQ CSV and a labelled test set. Everything else is roadmap.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: RISK 1, AI accuracy on mixed-language site chat. A false negative means missed money; false positives bury the PM in noise. Plan: build a labelled synthetic test set of 60-80 messages (code-switching, Chinese, abbreviations, voice-note transcripts) and report precision and recall in the pitch. Add a BQ glossary to the prompt ('PP = power point = 13A socket'). Every card shows its source text, low confidence goes to a manual queue, and nothing is sent without a human. Fallback during the demo: if the LLM API fails, fall back to keyword and regex rules plus cached AI outputs, and offer a manual 'Mark as instruction' button. RISK 2, getting messages in: no WhatsApp group API is assumed, so use chat export or forwarding. RISK 3, the main contractor will not sign. The status stays 'Sent, not confirmed', with the dated send record kept in the log. The product makes no claim about its legal effect.
ideas.business_model: Freemium on the Orbyte credit wallet. One active project free, with manual tagging and no AI. Paid tier: a per-active-project monthly credit bundle (our proposal: about RM39-59 per project per month; Orbyte publishes no RM prices) plus credits per signed VO, reusing Orbyte's per-signed-document unit. Price anchors: micro-firm accounting software such as Bukku costs RM0-135/month plus 8% SST (Bukku pricing page, fetched 2026-10-25), and one AIAC adjudication starts at RM3,036 in adjudicator fees alone. Partner channel: construction trade associations and accounting firms that serve contractors. Growth: homeowner-renovation variant, then other change-request-heavy sectors through the same module.

ideas.name: HoldBack Ledger: claim-to-cash, retention release and exposure tracker
ideas.one_liner: A rules engine over each subcontract. It tracks claimed, certified and paid amounts and the retention held. It fires owner-approved follow-ups and retention-release requests the day they fall due, and alerts the owner when money stuck with one main contractor passes a limit the owner set.
ideas.target_user: Owners and admin or account staff at micro and small B2B subcontractors (same trades as idea 1) running about 2-8 concurrent subcontracts, who track claims and retention in Excel or a notebook. Homeowner renovation is excluded from the core segment (CIPAA s.3). Evidence is for construction SMEs including medium firms; no source isolates micro firms.
ideas.trigger: SCHEDULE: a rules run every day at 08:00. EVENTS: certificate recorded, payment recorded, completion or defects date entered, promise-to-pay logged. Rule triggers: (1) Claim cut-off day, from the contract. If the user marks the contract as silent, the default is monthly, labelled 'statutory default, CIPAA s.36(3)(a); confirm with your contract'. (2) Payment due date passes without full payment. Contract term, or a labelled default of 30 calendar days from receipt of invoice (s.36(4)). (3) Retention milestone reached: practical completion, then end of the defects liability period (DLP months set per contract). (4) Exposure to one main contractor exceeds the owner's limit. (5) Certified amount falls more than 5% below claimed. Synthetic example: Kaca Jernih Aluminium & Glass Sdn Bhd (fictional, 14 staff, Seri Kembangan). The run on 24/10/2026 finds: (a) Warehouse office, Klang, under Gaya Mantap Construction (fictional): RM410,000, 5% retention. Completion was 30/09/2025 and the 12-month DLP ended 30/09/2026. The second half of retention, RM10,250, has not been requested (+24 days), and the CMGD copy is missing. (b) Residensi Seri Kenanga Block B under Mega Tiang Builders (fictional): Claim #7 was submitted 25/08/2026 for RM48,300 and certified at RM41,900 (under-certified by RM6,400). Net of 5% retention it is RM39,805, due 24/09/2026. RM20,000 was paid on 10/10, leaving RM19,805 outstanding, 30 days overdue. Mega Tiang accounts on WhatsApp: 'Boss, developer belum bayar kita, next month la ya.' (c) Mega Tiang exposure: RM85,705 against an owner limit of RM80,000.
ideas.connected_data: Orbyte Clients & Projects. Per-contract terms, 6 fields entered once or imported from Excel CSV: contract value, retention %, payment period, claim cut-off day, completion date, DLP months. Per-claim records: claimed, certified, retention deducted, payments received (from the accounting system via Orbyte Connect, mocked, or a bank-statement CSV). Documents in Orbyte storage: CPC, CMGD, certificates. PM's estimate of work done but not yet claimed. Promise-to-pay entries. Optional feed of confirmed VOs from idea 1. All demo data is synthetic.
ideas.decision_logic: Deterministic rules only, each showing its formula. RETENTION: when today is on or after the milestone date and no release has been requested, check prerequisite documents. If complete, draft a release invoice and cover letter. If missing, create a PM task with a template asking the main contractor for the certificate. OVERDUE LADDER: day 1 friendly reminder draft; day 14 statement-of-account draft; day 30 owner call task plus exposure-review flag. Drafts are never auto-sent. A logged promise-to-pay date pauses the ladder until that date, then it re-fires. UNDER-CERTIFICATION: certified more than 5% below claimed creates a QS task to record the reason or request a breakdown. EXPOSURE per main contractor = retention held + certified unpaid + claimed not certified + work done not claimed. Mega Tiang: RM21,500 (5% of RM430,000 cumulative certified) + RM19,805 + RM6,400 + RM38,000 = RM85,705, which exceeds the RM80,000 limit, so the owner is alerted. TREND: if average days-to-pay over the last 3 claims rose more than 15 days versus the previous 3, show an amber flag.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: Not needed, by design. Every number here is arithmetic on contract terms and dates, and owners must be able to check each alert by hand: explainability matters more than cleverness when money is chased. Possible later add-on outside the MVP: OCR or AI to prefill certified amounts from scanned interim certificates, still with human confirmation.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no LLM and no chat surface. It is a scheduled rules engine over a money ledger that feeds an approval inbox, outputs documents (release request, statement of account, draft invoice) and keeps an audit log. Judges see a 'money stuck' dashboard, a date simulator firing alerts, and an approve button that pushes a draft invoice to an accounting mock.
ideas.human_approval: Owner/Director (or a designated finance manager) approves three consequential actions. (a) Sending a retention-release request and pushing the draft release invoice to the accounting system. (b) Sending any reminder at ladder step 2 or above. (c) Recording a decision on an exposure breach, from options the owner defined: 'continue', 'hold new material POs for this project pending meeting', 'refer to adviser'. The product never recommends one. When deciding, the approver sees: the ledger breakdown with formula; the source of the contract term (the clause the user entered, or 'statutory default, contract marked silent'); attached CPC or CMGD; a message preview; promise-to-pay history; and the main contractor's days-to-pay over the last 6 claims.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated RBAC. OWNER/DIRECTOR: all projects and the company-wide exposure view; approves sends and invoice pushes; sets exposure limits, ladder timings and decision options. ADMIN/ACCOUNT CLERK: records certificates, payments and promise-to-pay dates; prepares drafts; may send step-1 reminders only; cannot push invoices or change limits. PROJECT MANAGER: own projects only; uploads CPC and CMGD; enters work-done estimates; cannot see company-wide exposure. EXTERNAL ACCOUNTANT: read-only ledger export and receipt of draft invoices through the connector. MAIN CONTRACTOR: receives documents only, with an optional eSign acknowledgment.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees a 'Money stuck' dashboard per main contractor. Kaca Jernih: retention held RM46,750 across 3 projects; certified overdue RM19,805; claimed not certified RM6,400. It includes a 90-day release calendar and an approval inbox. After approval, the release request shows 'Sent 24/10/2026', and the draft invoice appears in the accounting mock. Append-only log. 2026-10-24 08:00 RULE retention.release.due: Gaya Mantap / Klang, 2nd half RM10,250, milestone 30/09/2026 +24d, CMGD missing, task to Hafiz (PM). 08:00 RULE overdue.ladder step 3: Mega Tiang Claim #7 RM19,805, +30d. 08:00 RULE exposure.limit: Mega Tiang RM85,705 > RM80,000. 10:12 Priya (Admin) logged promise-to-pay 15/11/2026 (source: WhatsApp from Mega Tiang accounts); ladder paused. 14:30 Hafiz uploaded CMGD.pdf; rule re-run; INV-DRAFT-0931 RM10,250 created. 15:05 Mr Tan (Owner) approved; ENV-8120 sent; draft pushed as ACC-55410 (mocked). 15:07 Mr Tan exposure decision: 'hold new glass PO for Kenanga B until meeting 28/10'.
ideas.measurable_benefit: Sourced context. Retention is 'typically 5% to 10%' of contract value, 'often equivalent to several months of operating cash flow' (MCMEA seminar reported by Malaysia SME, 13 Jan 2026; an association estimate). Retention is not trust money unless the wording is clear and a separate fund exists (Federal Court, SK M&E Bersekutu 2019, per DNH 2023). It is generally lost if the main contractor becomes insolvent, so every day it stays held after its release date is unpaid exposure. Malaysian construction firms' average payment delay as payers (Experian iDTC) fell from 87 days in Q1 2024 to 76 days in Q4 2024. That is an improving trend, covers all sizes, and measures payment speed, not project delay. ESTIMATES to validate. (1) KPI: days from retention milestone to release request. Target: 3 working days or fewer, against today's unknown lag. No source measures that lag, so interviews must. The synthetic case surfaces RM10,250 that was 24 days late on day 1. (2) KPI: RM of certified amounts more than 30 days overdue, tracked monthly. (3) Follow-up admin time across 4 projects: from an estimated 3-4 hours a week to under 1 hour. (4) Exposure breaches seen before the next material PO, not after.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: Directly fits Orbyte's stated direction: a 'Business Graph' linking projects, invoices, payment terms and cash flow, and an AI example of 'follow up unpaid invoices'. This is the deterministic backbone for both. Reuses Clients & Projects, approval workflows with audit trail, eSign for release-request acknowledgment, and the credit wallet. Through Connect it uses the accounting category (Bukku, SQL or AutoCount, mocked) and, on the roadmap, the financing-referral category: a clean certified-receivables ledger can support referral to invoice-financing partners (referral only, no advice). It complements accounting rather than replacing it. Bukku already handles retention receivable, release invoices and auto-reminders on issued invoices (Grow plan, RM65/month). HoldBack adds the steps before an invoice exists: milestone dates and document prerequisites, under-certification gaps, and cross-project exposure per customer. Reusable building block: a 'Staged Billing & Holdback' rules API (contract-term template plus milestone events gives due dates, holdbacks, ladders and exposure). Other sectors: IT system integrators with UAT holdbacks, contract manufacturers with milestone payments, event and wedding vendors with deposit and balance stages, and maintenance contractors. It chains with idea 1 (confirmed VOs feed the claim ledger).
ideas.scope_check: Not HR/admin: B2B receivables, not staff claims, leave or payroll. No real payments: it only records payments imported from accounting or a bank CSV. No statutory filing: no CIPAA claims, notices or adjudication documents. A 'CIPAA-ready evidence export for your adviser' stays on the roadmap only. It deliberately does not run the payer's 10-working-day payment-response clock: that deadline binds the payer, and acting on it is legal process. Not legal or financial advice: s.36 defaults appear only as labelled defaults when the user marks the contract silent. It never advises suspension under s.29, adjudication or credit decisions; exposure limits and decision options are set by the owner. PDPA: mostly business data, plus names and phone numbers of the main contractor's staff. The demo is fully synthetic. Production uses role-based access, masks contacts in exports, sets a retention period per project, deletes on request and handles breaches under PDPA 2010 as amended in 2024.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: Build live: the daily rules run, driven by a 'simulate date' control over a seeded synthetic ledger (1 firm, 3-4 projects). Advance the date to 24/10/2026 and three explainable alerts land in the approval inbox: retention release due with a missing document, an overdue claim at ladder step 3, and an exposure breach. Upload the missing CMGD, the rule re-runs, and the owner approves. The app then generates a draft invoice as JSON for a mock accounting API, sets the status to Sent, and writes the log lines. Unit-test the rules. Dashboards beyond the 'money stuck' card are roadmap.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: RISK 1: judges or users see it as 'Bukku already does this', and data entry kills adoption. Plan: position it as a layer above accounting through Orbyte Connect, not a replacement. Keep the MVP to 6 contract fields and 3 numbers per claim, with an Excel CSV import. Validate in 3-5 subcontractor interviews that release lag and single-main-contractor exposure are real for them (no source quantifies either). Fallback: if the connector is not ready, export the draft invoice as PDF or CSV. RISK 2, demo: date-based triggers are invisible live, so use a 'simulate date' control and seeded data, with rules covered by unit tests so the run is deterministic. RISK 3: wrong contract terms produce wrong alerts. Every alert shows its term source and formula, and nothing is sent without approval.
ideas.business_model: Freemium on the Orbyte credit wallet: 2 active projects free. Premium per active project (our proposal: about RM29-49 per project per month; Orbyte publishes no RM prices), or transaction credits per approved release request or reminder sent. Partner revenue on the roadmap: referral fees through Connect's financing-referral category for certified receivables, and an accounting-firm channel for contractors. Price anchor: micro firms already pay Bukku RM0-135/month plus 8% SST for accounting. Growth: bundle with VO Catcher as a 'Subcontractor Cash Pack', then non-construction staged-billing templates.

ideas.name: SahBayar Gate: payment-verified release for orders
ideas.one_liner: A release lock for cash-before-delivery orders. Staff cannot ship, load or hand over goods until a matching credit appears in the business's own bank or gateway records, or the owner approves an exception. All four known fake-proof tricks fail by default, and nobody has to judge whether a screenshot is real.
ideas.target_user:
The target is small B2B suppliers and wholesalers (frozen food, dry goods, hardware, packaging) and chat sellers with 2-15 staff. In these businesses the person who releases goods (sales admin, storekeeper, packer, driver) is not the person who can see the bank account (the owner). They take WhatsApp or phone orders, are paid by bank transfer or DuitNow, and release goods on cash-before-delivery. Evidence fit (all figures as corrected by the verifiers):
- Utusan, 2025-10-06: a syndicate hit supplier companies in 8 cases totalling RM221,853.80. The method was a phone order, a fake receipt, then goods collected by hired transport.
- Kosmo, 2025-05-31 (allegation): a kunafa business's staff accepted edited receipts from a personal shopper for 8 months.
- The Vibes, 2025-09-17: a Port Dickson RM780 loss was found only after the worker spoke to the employer.
- Bernama, 2025-04-21: police advice is that 'all transactions should be verified through official banking systems before releasing goods'. This product puts that advice into the workflow.
It deliberately does not target 1-2 person hawkers, because a soundbox (RM179-RM239 from Qashier) already covers a QR counter where the owner is present.
ideas.trigger:
Main trigger (event): a staff member tries to move a cash-before-delivery order to 'released' (print the DO, mark it packed or shipped, confirm a lorry pickup).

Synthetic day at Sinar Jaya Frozen Food Trading (fictional; Klang; 9 staff):
- 10:02, WhatsApp from Ah Keong Mini Market: 'Boss, order 20 ctn nugget + 10 ctn sosej. Dah transfer RM1,248, ni resit ya' [screenshot]. The sales admin creates order SJ-1043 and attaches the screenshot as the customer's CLAIM, not as proof.
- At confirmation, SahBayar produces a ready-to-copy reply: 'Jumlah RM1,248.00. Sila taip rujukan SJ1043 semasa transfer.'
- 11:40, phone call from a new customer, 'Mega Runcit Enterprise': 'Saya ambil 60 ctn, lorry saya datang pukul 3, resit saya WhatsApp sekarang'. This becomes order SJ-1047 for RM4,860, with a 'DuitNow Berjaya' screenshot attached.
- Kak Ros Catering sends a receipt for order SJ-1045 (RM312.00).

Secondary trigger: each new credit batch (bank CSV upload or gateway webhook) re-runs matching for every held order.
ideas.connected_data:
1. Order record: customer, items, total, payment terms, and release method (self-pickup, third-party transport or courier).
2. Customer record from Orbyte's clients master: first order or repeat, past matched payments, and whether the customer is on credit terms.
3. Credit records, normalised into one table (date-time, amount, payer name, reference, source transaction id). Sources:
   - (a) the bank's CSV export, uploaded by the owner. The Maybank2u Biz app's App Store listing (Malayan Banking Berhad, fetched 2026-10-25) advertises 'Export Transactions as CSV File'. Other banks' export formats were not verified.
   - (b) a payment-gateway webhook through an Orbyte Connect 'payments and collections' partner;
   - (c) the owner's one-tap 'seen in my bank app' confirmation.
4. Per-business rule settings: time window, RM thresholds, trusted-customer list.

The customer's screenshot is stored only as a claim and is never treated as evidence of payment.
ideas.decision_logic:
Deterministic rules. The first rule that fires wins, and each result shows its rule id in plain words.
- R1 VERIFIED: there is an unused credit that carries the order reference, or that is at least the order total and comes from the customer's name, inside the time window (order time minus 1h to plus 48h). Result: green, release unlocked for staff, credit marked as used.
- R2 SHORT: a credit links to the order but is below the total. Result: red, with the shortfall shown. This catches the 1-sen edit and 'only half came in'.
- R3 ALREADY USED: the only candidate credit has already been used by another order (same transaction id). Result: red, 'proof reused'.
- R4 NO CREDIT YET: nothing matches. Result: amber, staff cannot release, and the owner is notified with the RM at risk. This covers request-for-money screens, edited receipts and swapped QR stickers, because in all three no money reaches the business account.
- R5 HIGH-RISK RELEASE: new customer, order above a threshold (default RM2,000) and third-party pickup. Result: no override allowed; release only on R1. This is the Utusan syndicate pattern.
- R6 CREDIT TERMS: the customer is flagged as on terms. Result: routed to the owner to approve release on credit, recorded as a receivable.
Credits with no order are listed for the owner.

Worked example: the 10:30 CSV upload contains 'DUITNOW CR SJ1043 TAN AH KEONG 1,248.00', so SJ-1043 passes R1 and goes green. SJ-1045 finds a credit of RM0.01 with reference SJ1045, so R2 reports 'SHORT RM311.99'. For SJ-1047, the 14:45 upload has no credit between RM4,850 and RM4,870 since 11:00, so R4 and R5 fire. When the lorry arrives at 15:00, the storekeeper's screen reads 'Bayaran belum masuk. Jangan muat barang.'
ideas.where_ai_adds_value:
AI is deliberately left out of the core.
- Every check here (amount at least the total, reference equals the order code, transaction id not reused, time window, RM threshold) is exact. Each check must be explainable to a non-technical owner and to an auditor, and a probabilistic model would add doubt where certainty is available.
- All the documented tricks (edited receipts, 1-sen transfers, request-for-money screens, reused proof, swapped QR stickers) fail the same test: no matching credit reaches the account. The gate never needs to judge the image.
- One optional later step is fuzzy payer-name matching when the customer leaves out the reference. That is Concept 2's job, kept outside the gate so the gate stays deterministic and auditable.
- Saying this openly also answers the rubric's 'AI only where it adds value'.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no conversation anywhere in the product. It is a state machine on each order (Claimed, Held, then Verified, Short or Reused, then Released) with a lock on the release button, a visible rules table and an approval queue. The only text it produces is a fixed-template payment message with a reference code. In the demo, judges see a storekeeper's button stay red while the 'lorry' waits and an owner approval screen, not a chat window.
ideas.roles_and_permissions:
Simulated login with a role switcher, built on Orbyte's existing roles and approval workflow.
- Owner: everything. Sets rules and thresholds, uploads statements, approves overrides of any size, sees all credits.
- Finance/Admin: uploads statements, matches manually, approves overrides up to the RM limit, sees credits.
- Sales admin: creates orders, attaches claims, sends the payment-reference message. Sees each order's status only (Verified, Short, Held), never bank lines, balances or other customers' payer names.
- Storekeeper, packer or driver: sees a release list with green or red only. Can mark goods released only when the order is green or owner-approved.
- External accountant: read-only access to the log and the matched-credit report.
The separation of duties is the product: whoever releases goods cannot also confirm the payment.
ideas.outcome_and_log:
What users see:
- SJ-1043 shows 'Payment verified: DUITNOW CR 10:28, RM1,248.00, rule R1', and the DO prints with a verification stamp.
- SJ-1045 shows 'SHORT RM311.99', and the sales admin gets a template message asking the customer for the balance.
- SJ-1047 stays locked. The owner rejects it, and sales gets a neutral reply to send: 'Maaf, kami hanya lepaskan barang selepas bayaran masuk ke akaun syarikat.'
- An end-of-day 'Claimed vs received' panel shows RM claimed, RM verified, RM released on terms, RM held or blocked, and credits with no order.

What the activity log records (append-only, exportable as CSV for the accountant): timestamp, user, role, action, order, status before and after, rule id, credit source (file name and row, or webhook id), screenshot hash, and the override reason.
ideas.measurable_benefit:
All figures below are estimates for validation with SME owners. No aggregate figure exists for merchant losses.
- Loss avoided per blocked syndicate-style release: Utusan (2025-10-06) reports 8 supplier cases totalling RM221,853.80, about RM27,700 per case on average (our division). Blocking one such release outweighs years of usage fees.
- Insider or agent pattern: the kunafa allegation is RM246,611 over about 8 months (Kosmo, 2025-05-31), roughly RM30,800 a month. With the gate, a non-owner cannot release goods against an unmatched receipt at all, so exposure shrinks to owner-approved overrides.
- Owner time (assumption): 40 transfer orders a day at 1-2 minutes each to check the bank app is 40-80 minutes a day. Batch upload with auto-match leaves only the exceptions, about 10-15 minutes a day.
- Demo KPIs: share of released RM backed by a matched credit (target at least 95%), RM held at risk, and median minutes from claim to verified.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse:
It reuses what Orbyte already ships instead of duplicating it:
- Orbyte features used: platform review-and-approval with audit trail, roles and access control, and the clients master.
- Connect categories: credits come in through 'payments and collections' (gateway webhooks) and orders through 'e-commerce and POS'.
- Write-back: the verified payment is written to the accounting system of record through the 'accounting' category. That follows Orbyte's stated pattern of writing approved results back.
- Roadmap fit: it fills the money-side white space on Orbyte's roadmap (the 'Business Graph' linking invoices, payment terms and cash flow).

Reusable building blocks:
1. Payment Match API: POST /claims, POST /credits, GET /orders/{id}/release-status.
2. Credit-source adapters (bank CSV parser per bank, gateway webhook, manual confirm), shared with Concept 2.
3. Rule packs per sector. The engine stays the same and only the release step changes:
   - online seller: ship the parcel;
   - wholesaler: load the lorry;
   - car workshop: hand back the car;
   - printer or creative studio: start the job or release the files;
   - caterer: confirm the event date after the deposit.
ideas.scope_check:
- Not HR or admin: this is sales and receivables control, outside Orbyte's People modules.
- No real payments: it only reads credit records. It never starts, moves, refunds or holds money, and it is not a payment gateway. It holds goods, not funds.
- No statutory filing.
- No legal or financial advice: labels say 'payment not received', never 'fraud', and reporting to police stays the owner's decision.
- PDPA (2010, as amended 2024): payer names and account numbers are personal data.
  - They are collected only to verify payment, and that purpose is stated in the order message template.
  - Account numbers are masked to the last 4 digits, and screenshots are kept as a hash plus a thumbnail.
  - Retention is configurable (default 12 months), access is limited by role, and data stays inside the SME's Orbyte tenant.
- Demo data: synthetic orders, a synthetic CSV and fictional bank names only.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback:
Risk 1: the credit feed.
- We found no verified open-banking account-information feed for micro or small business accounts in Malaysia. This is unverified either way.
- Fallback, in order:
  - (a) the owner uploads the bank's CSV export (the Maybank2u Biz app listing advertises CSV export; other banks not checked);
  - (b) a gateway webhook for sellers already using payment links;
  - (c) the owner's one-tap 'seen in bank app' confirmation, which still enforces separation of duties and the audit log.
- The demo runs entirely on synthetic CSV, so it depends on neither live Orbyte nor any bank.

Risk 2: adoption against cheaper existing fixes.
- Soundboxes cost RM179-RM239 from Qashier, and payment links cost about RM1 or 1% per transaction (ToyyibPay).
- Answer: target remote and staff-released orders that soundboxes do not cover, and accept gateway confirmations as one more credit source. Nudge repeat 'screenshot' customers toward payment links instead of competing with them.

Risk 3: friction while waiting for an upload.
- Answer: a trusted-customer credit-terms list, upload reminders before pickup times, and owner manual-match from the phone.
ideas.business_model:
- Pricing model: usage-based through Orbyte's credit wallet, with no per-seat fees, matching Orbyte's model.
- Freemium: the first ~50 verified releases a month are free.
- Transaction: after that, a per-verified-release charge (indicatively RM0.10-0.20; an assumption to test with SMEs).
- Premium: multi-branch, custom rule packs and accountant exports.
- Partner: referral revenue from Orbyte Connect payment-link and gateway partners when the tool converts screenshot customers to hosted payment links. Bank CSV adapters could be co-built with accounting partners.
- Growth path: wholesalers, then online sellers with packers, then service businesses (workshops, printers, caterers) using the same engine.

ideas.name: TutupKira AI: nightly claimed-vs-received close
ideas.one_liner: Every night an agent reads all the payment screenshots staff collected that day, from any bank or e-wallet and in BM, English or Chinese. It matches each claim against what actually reached the bank and gives the owner one review screen of gaps, each with a polite follow-up draft. A leak is caught the next morning instead of months later.
ideas.target_user:
The target is micro and small businesses where payment proof arrives as screenshots across many WhatsApp chats and several staff phones, and nobody reconciles. Examples: bakeries and kuih or catering businesses with pre-orders, F&B with two or more tills or shifts, retail shops, bazaar operators with helpers, businesses selling through resellers or runners, and service businesses that collect monthly fees by transfer (tuition centres, kindergartens).

Evidence fit:
- Kosmo, 2025-05-31 (allegation): a kunafa business's staff accepted edited receipts from a personal shopper for about 8 months before anyone noticed.
- SAYS, 2025-03-13: a bazaar kuih stall, 'Cuma separuh je yang masuk', and a nasi kerabu seller who accepted reused payment proof.
- Kosmo, 2025-03-04: in the Jerantut murtabak case an honest QR payment failed, was noticed only after breaking fast, and was paid once the customer found out. This shows the value of a routine follow-up, not fraud.
ideas.trigger:
Schedule plus event.
- During the day, staff forward each payment screenshot to the shop's Orbyte inbox. Alternatively, someone uploads a WhatsApp 'Export chat' file at closing, which needs no API.
- At closing time (for example 22:30), or when the owner uploads the day's bank CSV, the agent runs the daily close.

Synthetic day at Kek & Kuih Mak Teh (fictional; Seremban; 6 staff; 1 counter, WhatsApp pre-orders, 2 resellers). Messages in the day's chats:
- 'Kak, nak 3 bekas kuih lapis + 1 kek batik utk Sabtu. Dah transfer RM135 ya, resit attached'
- '老板，我已经转账 RM88 了，请查收'
- 'Boss dah bank in liao, semalam punya + hari ni sekali, total RM210'
- 'Liza (agent)' sends 5 receipts for bulk orders worth RM1,460.
In total there are 47 claims worth RM3,846.40.
ideas.connected_data:
1. Claims: payment screenshots plus the chat text around them (customer, items, amount stated, 'sekali' combined payments).
2. Credits: the bank's CSV export or statement (the Maybank2u Biz app listing advertises CSV export; other banks not verified), and gateway settlement reports through Orbyte Connect 'payments and collections'.
3. Sales: the pre-order sheet or POS daily totals through 'e-commerce and POS'.
4. Orbyte clients master: customer and reseller names, phone contacts, and each one's past matching history.
5. The shop's own receiving account(s), used to check who the screenshot says was paid.
ideas.decision_logic:
The decision runs in two layers. The AI layer reads and proposes; a rules layer decides each status.

AI layer:
- extracts each claim's fields and classifies the screen type;
- links chat text to claims and orders;
- proposes candidate credit(s) with a confidence score and a one-line reason.

Rules layer:
- MATCHED: credit is at least the claimed amount, inside the window, and not used before.
- SHORT: credit is below the claim.
- NO CREDIT: no credit found.
- DUPLICATE PROOF: same image perceptual hash or same transaction reference as an earlier claim.
- NOT A PAYMENT: the screen is a request-for-money, pending or failed screen.
- WRONG RECIPIENT: the last 4 digits of the recipient account differ from the shop's account (catches a swapped QR sticker).
- UNCLAIMED CREDIT: money arrived with no claim.
Anything below confidence 0.9, or any discrepancy, goes to a human. A pattern rule suggests 'verify-first' for any customer or reseller with two or more unmatched claims in 7 days.

Synthetic results:
- 43 claims MATCHED, RM3,109.40. This includes one RM210 transfer correctly split across 2 orders, and the Chinese RM88 claim matched to a credit from a different family name ('dibayar oleh suami').
- 'Liza (agent)': 2 of 5 claims have NO CREDIT (RM480 + RM160 = RM640). The nearest credit is RM4.80 from LIZA at 14:11.
- 1 DUPLICATE PROOF of RM45: the same image as Tuesday's.
- 1 NOT A PAYMENT of RM52: a 'DuitNow Request' screen.
- 1 UNCLAIMED CREDIT of RM25.
Issues total RM737.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value:
AI is used in steps 2-3, in three places where rules do badly.

1. Reading the screenshot.
- Screens come from dozens of bank, e-wallet and DuitNow layouts, in BM, English or Chinese, and are often cropped, compressed or forwarded.
- Template OCR needs one rule set per layout and breaks whenever an app changes its design.
- A vision model extracts amount, time, reference, recipient and sender. It also classifies the screen type ('successful transfer' vs 'request for money' vs 'pending'). The Port Dickson RM780 loss came from exactly this confusion (The Vibes, 2025-09-17).
- It is the same kind of capability Orbyte already ships for eClaim receipt reading, pointed at customer payments.

2. Linking messy text to money.
- One transfer can cover two orders ('semalam punya + hari ni sekali').
- A spouse may pay ('suami saya yang bayar').
- Bank descriptors like 'DUITNOW CR 1022 NUR AISYAH BT' must be tied to a WhatsApp contact saved as 'Kak Aisyah Kuih Raya'.
- Exact-string rules miss these cases and raise false alarms that owners learn to ignore.

3. Drafting a polite, non-accusatory follow-up in the customer's own language.

What AI deliberately does NOT do: decide fraud, or judge whether an image is edited. Fakes 'can be easily generated using AI' (Yayasan Digital Malaysia COO, Bernama, 2025-03-24), so image forensics is unreliable. The bank credit is the only proof. The AI turns messy evidence into rows that deterministic rules can check.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: Nobody talks to it. It is a scheduled batch agent: the input is a pile of images, chat exports and a bank ledger. The output is a reconciliation table with statuses, a review queue and draft messages. The owner's only actions are Approve, Edit or Skip on each row. Judges see a side-by-side 'claim vs bank line' screen with the extracted fields highlighted on the image, plus a morning summary card. There is no text box to type questions into.
ideas.human_approval:
The Owner (or a Supervisor up to a set RM limit) approves four kinds of consequential action:
- (a) Any AI match below the confidence threshold, and any match that would turn a discrepancy into 'matched'.
- (b) Every customer follow-up before it goes out. The draft is shown in BM, English or Chinese with Edit, Send or Skip. Send opens WhatsApp click-to-chat with the text prefilled, and the human presses send. Asking a customer about missing money affects the relationship, so it is never automatic.
- (c) Marking a customer or reseller 'verify-first', which links to Concept 1's release gate.
- (d) Closing the day, which locks it for the accountant.

What the approver sees:
- the screenshot with extracted fields highlighted on the image, and the bank line(s) beside it;
- the rule result and the AI confidence;
- a one-line reason, for example: 'Screenshot: RM480.00, 14:12, to MAK TEH ENT. Bank: no credit RM470-490 between 13:00-18:00; nearest is RM4.80 from LIZA at 14:11.'

Example draft: 'Salam Kak Aisyah, terima kasih atas order semalam (3 bekas kuih lapis). Kami belum nampak bayaran RM135 masuk ke akaun kedai. Boleh tolong semak dengan bank akak? Terima kasih!'
ideas.roles_and_permissions:
Simulated in the demo with a role switcher on Orbyte roles.
- Owner: everything. Approves follow-ups, verify-first flags and the day close. Sees all bank lines.
- Supervisor/Admin: reviews matches, edits drafts, and approves follow-ups up to a set RM limit. Cannot change flags or close the day.
- Counter or sales staff: forward or upload claims, and see whether their own shift's claims matched. Never see bank lines, balances or other customers' details.
- External accountant: read-only access to closed days and exports.
Results are grouped by till or shift for cash-up only, never as staff performance scores. This keeps the product clear of HR.
ideas.measurable_benefit:
All figures below are estimates for validation with SME owners. No aggregate figure exists for merchant losses.
- Detection lag falls from months to under 24 hours. In the kunafa allegation (RM246,611 over about 8 months, Kosmo, 2025-05-31) that is roughly RM1,000 a day on average (our division). A nightly close would flag the pattern after the first unmatched day, so exposure plausibly drops to a few days rather than eight months.
- Honest misses are recovered routinely. The murtabak RM400 was repaid once the customer knew; a nightly follow-up makes that systematic instead of luck.
- Owner time (assumption): 40-50 screenshot payments a day at about 1 minute each to check against the bank app is 40-50 minutes. Reviewing exceptions only takes an estimated 5-10 minutes. Curlec's claim that manual reconciliation becomes 'a part-time job' at around 50 orders a day is unsourced vendor copy, cited as context only.
- Demo KPIs: extraction accuracy on the synthetic set (target at least 95% on amount and time fields), share of claims auto-matched, RM flagged, and hours from sale to detection.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse:
It extends a capability Orbyte already ships, AI receipt reading and policy flags in eClaim, from staff expenses to customer payments. That is new money-side capability, not a copy of HR.
- Orbyte features used: approval with audit trail, roles, and the clients master.
- Data in: credits from Connect 'payments and collections' and 'accounting', and sales from 'e-commerce and POS'.
- Data out: the closed day's matched receipts are posted to the accounting system of record.
- Roadmap fit: it is a working instance of Orbyte's own stated AI example, 'follow up unpaid invoices', and it feeds the planned Business Graph's cash-flow view.

Reusable building blocks:
- Payment Proof Reader API: image in, claim JSON out, with screen type and confidence.
- Bank Statement Normaliser: CSV or PDF in, credit rows out.
- Reconciliation Engine, shared with Concept 1.
- A follow-up template library per language.

Cross-sector uses:
- bakery pre-orders and F&B tills;
- tuition-centre and kindergarten monthly fees paid by parents' screenshots;
- workshop and catering deposits;
- reseller and agent networks.
ideas.scope_check:
- Not HR or admin: this is cash reconciliation of sales, with no staff scoring.
- No real payments: it never moves, refunds or collects money.
- Follow-ups are reminders a human sends, not legal demands or debt collection.
- No fraud determination and no police filing. The owner can export an evidence pack for their own use.
- No statutory filing and no financial advice.
- PDPA (2010, as amended 2024): screenshots contain names and account numbers.
  - Use is limited to payment verification, and that purpose is stated in the shop's order message.
  - Account numbers are masked to the last 4 digits after extraction.
  - Images are kept for a short configurable period (default 90 days), then only the hash and extracted fields remain.
  - The AI provider is configured not to train on the data.
  - If the model runs outside Malaysia, check the cross-border transfer conditions in PDPA s.129.
  - Access is role-based.
- Demo data: synthetic screenshots using fictional bank and e-wallet names only.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback:
Risk 1: extraction accuracy on unfamiliar layouts.
- Anything uncertain, and any discrepancy, goes to the human queue.
- Fields are highlighted on the image for a two-second check.
- Rules re-check amount and time against the bank line. A misread amount therefore shows as a mismatch for review, never as a false 'matched'.

Risk 2: the credit feed (same as Concept 1).
- Fallbacks: bank CSV export upload, gateway settlement reports, and the owner's manual confirm.
- No verified open-banking feed for micro accounts in Malaysia was found.

Risk 3: a wrong output hurts a customer relationship.
- No message leaves without human approval, and drafts are neutral ('kami belum nampak bayaran masuk'), never accusing.

Risk 4: staff do not forward screenshots.
- A WhatsApp 'Export chat' upload at closing works with no API.

Demo fallback: pre-computed results if the live model call fails.
ideas.business_model:
- Pricing model: Orbyte's credit wallet, usage-based.
- Freemium: about 100 proofs a month free.
- Transaction: after that, a charge per proof read or per daily close (indicatively a few sen per proof; an assumption to validate).
- Premium: multiple outlets, a reseller/agent module and accountant export.
- Partners: bookkeepers and accountants who want clean daily receipts are the channel, plus referral revenue from payment-link partners for customers who keep paying by screenshot.
- Growth path: detection (nightly close) is the entry product. Customers it flags lead naturally to prevention (Concept 1's release gate), so the two sell as a ladder on one shared reconciliation engine.

ideas.name: Tempoh: a cross-agency obligation engine with threshold watch and professional hand-off
ideas.one_liner: A versioned rules engine reads the business profile and connected data from Orbyte. It works out every dated statutory and premises obligation, puts the cost of each day's delay in ringgit, and spots threshold crossings (SST, e-invoice) before they happen. It then collects the right documents and passes a director-approved pack to the company secretary, accountant or tax agent who files. Tempoh does not file anything itself.
ideas.target_user: Owner-directors and the one or two admin staff of upper-small Sdn Bhd firms with rented premises, especially SST-registered service firms (the verifiers judged this the segment where the pain survives). A lighter rule pack serves micro sole proprietors, covering council licence, signboard licence and tenancy stamping only. A secondary user is the external company secretary or accountant who receives the packs.
ideas.trigger: Three triggers, all automatic. (1) A daily 08:00 schedule re-computes every obligation and fires escalating reminders at 60, 30 and 7 days, the pattern 3E CPA recommends (24 Aug 2026). (2) Business events: a tenancy is signed by both parties on Orbyte eSign, the accounting connector syncs new invoices, or a premises record changes. (3) A rule-pack change, for example the LHDN release of 30 Aug 2026 raising the e-invoice exemption from RM1m to RM3m. The change re-computes obligations for every affected tenant. Synthetic example: SejukPro Aircond Services Sdn Bhd (fictional; 14 staff; Setapak shoplot; new Cheras store; SST-registered). On 9 Oct 2026 the Cheras tenancy is signed on eSign, which starts the stamp-duty clock. On 25 Oct the daily run sends owner Daniel Lim a WhatsApp digest: "Morning boss Daniel. 3 deadlines coming: (1) Stamp duty Cheras tenancy by 8 Nov, 14 days left. Signed TA [ok from eSign], landlord IC/SSM no [missing]. (2) SST-02 Sep-Oct by 30 Nov. Tax est RM11,600 from accounts sync. Late 1-30 days = +RM1,160. (3) SSM annual return by 12 Dec. Pn Rozita (cosec) waiting for you to confirm director address. Reply 1/2/3 for details." Daniel replies: "2 - ok send to Mr Tan accountant, but Sept got 2 invoice cancel, check first ya."
ideas.connected_data: (a) Orbyte org profile: entity type (Sdn Bhd or sole proprietor), incorporation date (12 Nov 2019), FYE (30 Jun), directors, SST registration flag. (b) Premises register, a new object inside the hub: council (DBKL), business licence number and expiry (31 Dec 2026), signboard licence, and the compound status flag. (c) Orbyte eSign (Documenso) audit log, which gives the exact both-parties-signed timestamp of the tenancy. (d) Orbyte Connect accounting or POS connector, synthetic in the demo: invoices, cancellations and a rolling 12-month revenue of RM2.78m. (e) Professional contacts: company secretary, tax agent, accountant. (f) The rule pack: rules stored as data, each with a source URL, an effective date and a last-verified date.
ideas.decision_logic: Deterministic rules only. Every computed date shows the rule ID, the rule-pack version and the source link. Example rules: SSM annual return due 30 days after the incorporation anniversary (3E CPA, 26 Aug 2026), so 12 Nov plus 30 days gives 12 Dec 2026. Form C due 7 months after FYE, giving 31 Jan 2027. SST-02 due on the last day of the month after the taxable period, giving 30 Nov 2026 for Sep-Oct. Tenancy stamping due within 30 days of execution (Ecovis, 9 Jul 2025): eSign 9 Oct gives 8 Nov 2026. A secondary 2026 guide (Speedhome) says the clock starts when both parties sign; this is not verified against LHDN. Licence renewal: DBKL multi-year renewal requires no compounds or rent arrears (Utusan, 20 May 2026), so an open compound marks the renewal BLOCKED. Threshold watch: if rolling 12-month revenue reaches 90% of the RM3m e-invoice exemption (LHDN, 30 Aug 2026) or of an SST registration threshold, the rules raise a 're-check status with your accountant' task. They never state 'you must register'. Cost of delay: the RMCD penalty schedule (10% for days 1-30, a further 15% for days 31-60, a further 15% for days 61-90, 40% maximum) applied to the synthetic tax of RM11,600 gives RM1,160, RM2,900 and RM4,640. The SSM s68 compound is shown as RM5,000 normally and RM500 under the 2026 reduction, which SSM's homepage headline says runs to 31 Dec 2026. Each obligation carries a document checklist; missing items become requests to the owner or admin.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: AI is not needed for the core. Dates, thresholds and penalties are published rules, and determinism is the selling point: every date is reproducible and cites its source. The only optional AI touch, left on the roadmap, would draft a plain-language note summarising a rule-pack change. A human curator still approves the rule itself. The product deliberately contrasts with Concept 2.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no free-text question-and-answer anywhere. The core is a rules engine that turns business data into a dated, sourced obligation register and a state machine: Due, Docs Missing, Pack Ready, Released, Filed by Professional, Closed. WhatsApp only carries notifications and numbered replies. The demo moment is a rule change, RM1m to RM3m, re-computing obligations for two synthetic firms and showing the diff. That is not something a chatbot does.
ideas.human_approval: (1) The director approves 'Release pack to external professional', for example the SST-02 prep pack to the fictional Tan & Co tax agent. The approval screen shows the obligation, due date and days left; the rule ID, version and source link; the figures and the invoice records behind them, including the two cancelled September invoices Daniel flagged, now excluded and marked; the document list; the recipient; which personal-data fields leave the business (IC numbers masked); and the ringgit cost of delay. (2) Closing an obligation takes two keys. The professional marks it 'Filed by professional' and uploads the reference or receipt. The director then accepts the closure. (3) A rule-pack change needs two people: a platform rule curator proposes it with the source document, and a partner accountant approves it before it reaches any tenant. Tenants see a 'Rule changed' banner with the affected dates.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated RBAC on Orbyte's existing roles and approval workflow. Director/Owner: views everything, edits the business profile, approves external release, accepts closure. Admin staff: views assigned obligations, uploads documents and answers checklists, but cannot release packs outside the company or close obligations. External professional (company secretary, accountant or tax agent) is a scoped guest who sees only packs released to them; they can comment, mark 'Filed by professional' with evidence, or mark 'Not applicable' with a reason that the director must accept. Rule curator (platform): proposes rule versions, has no tenant data access, and cannot self-approve. Read-only viewer (roadmap): for example, a lender receiving a director-approved good-standing summary through Orbyte Connect's financing-referral category.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees a single obligation timeline across SSM, LHDN, RMCD, the council and tenancy. Each obligation shows a status chip, days left, the ringgit cost of delay, and a green, amber or red good-standing summary. After approval, Daniel gets a WhatsApp message: "SST-02 pack sent to Tan & Co 10:42. 2 cancelled invoices excluded. Waiting for agent to confirm filing." The append-only activity log records: obligation computed (rule ID, pack version, input values, timestamp); each reminder sent (channel, recipient); each document uploaded (by whom, file hash); pack released (approver, recipient, file hashes, personal-data fields disclosed); professional marked filed (reference, evidence hash); director accepted closure; and any rule-change re-computation (old date, new date, rule version).
ideas.measurable_benefit: ESTIMATES, to be validated with SME owners. (1) Money kept, using primary-source penalty rates on synthetic amounts: avoiding one SST period filed 1-30 days late saves 10% of tax due, RM1,160 on RM11,600 and up to RM4,640 at the 40% cap (RMCD MySST penalties page). Avoiding one SSM s68 compound saves RM5,000 at the normal rate, or RM500 under the 2026 reduction (Acclime, 18 May 2026; SSM homepage headline, 9 Oct 2026). Tenancy stamping late penalties start at RM50 or 10% (Ecovis). Keeping a DBKL licence renewable keeps the premises legally operating (Utusan, 20 May 2026). (2) Time: our estimate is 1-2 owner or admin hours per obligation spent working out what is needed and chasing documents. Across 12-15 dated obligations a year for an SST-registered Sdn Bhd with premises, that falls to about 15 minutes each, roughly 15-25 hours a year saved. The only quantitative anchor is dated: IDEAS 2019 found corporate tax compliance took '44 days of staff time' in 120 micro and small service firms. (3) Pilot metrics: share of obligations Pack Ready 7 or more days before the due date; lead time between a threshold alert and the crossing; zero obligations closed without professional evidence.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: Tempoh fills white space Orbyte has named but not built: the money and compliance side, and the stated 'Business Graph' linking contracts, invoices and cash flow. It reuses Orbyte's platform-wide approval workflow and audit trail, roles, eSign (Documenso) audit timestamps, and the Connect categories for accounting and POS. Every approved result goes back as a record, matching Orbyte's 'approved results written back' pattern. It is reusable because rules are data, not code. A new council, state, sector or rule change means new rule rows with a source and effective date, and the same engine serves an F&B sole proprietor (licence, signboard, tenancy only) and an SST-registered services Sdn Bhd (full pack). The reusable block is an Obligation API that any Orbyte module or partner app can call: POST /events (for example tenancy.signed or revenue.synced) and GET /obligations?status=due. Partner company-secretary and accounting firms get a multi-client console of their SME clients' released packs.
ideas.scope_check: Not HR or admin. It contains no employee data and does not overlap eLeave, eClaim, eOT or Attendance. It covers business-level obligations to SSM, LHDN, RMCD, councils and landlords. No statutory filing: it prepares and hands off, and the professional files through MBRS, MySST or e-Duti Setem. No real payments: penalties appear only as a cost-of-delay estimate. No legal or tax advice: dates come from published rules with citations, threshold alerts say 're-check with your accountant', and questions like 'does this apply to me?' route to the named professional. PDPA: the demo uses synthetic data only. In production, personal data is limited to director and landlord names and IC or registration numbers (stored masked except where a pack needs them). Uploaders see a purpose notice. Any disclosure to a third party needs director approval and is logged. Access is role-based, records follow retention rules (7 years for stamp-duty records, per Ecovis), and data can be exported or deleted where the law requires no retention.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: Build the versioned rule engine (about 8 rules from verified sources) and one full journey on it. The Cheras tenancy is signed on simulated eSign, the engine creates a stamp-by date of 8 Nov with its source cited, and the missing document is requested. The admin uploads it. The director sees the approval screen and releases the pack to the simulated company secretary. The secretary marks it filed with evidence, the director accepts, and the activity log shows the whole chain. Live stretch: switch the e-invoice rule from RM1m to RM3m and show re-computed obligations for two synthetic firms. This proves reuse and explainability.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: Risk 1: a stale or wrong rule produces a wrong date. The e-invoice threshold alone moved several times in 2025-2026, and a 3E CPA calendar dated 6 Sep 2026 was already outdated. Fallbacks: every rule carries a source URL, effective date and last-verified date, and changes need two people. Where a rule is ambiguous the engine uses the earliest plausible date. Every output reads 'prepared for your professional to confirm'. The MVP uses only rules verified from primary or clearly cited sources (RMCD penalties, the LHDN 30 Aug 2026 release, SSM). Risk 2: judges see 'a calendar the company secretary already provides', a point the verifiers raised. Answer: company secretaries cover SSM, and free calendars such as Lookuptax exclude direct-tax and company-registry deadlines. Nobody joins premises licences, tenancy stamping, SST and connected-revenue threshold watching with a document hand-off. We will validate this with 5 owners and 1 company secretary before the final. Technical fallback: if connectors are not ready, import synthetic invoices by CSV.
ideas.business_model: Fits Orbyte's credit wallet with no per-seat fees, as proposed tiers (Orbyte publishes no RM prices). Free: the obligation calendar and reminders for one entity on the core rule pack, as an acquisition hook. Usage: one credit per released hand-off pack or closed obligation, matching Orbyte's per-claim and per-signed-document charging. Premium: threshold watch from connected revenue, multi-premises, multi-entity. Partner: company-secretary, accounting and tax-agent firms run a multi-client console, with revenue share for firms that bring their SME clients onto Orbyte. Roadmap partner revenue: a director-approved good-standing summary for Orbyte Connect's financing-referral category.

ideas.name: Surat Masuk: an AI reader that turns official documents into verified deadlines
ideas.one_liner: The owner forwards a photo or PDF of any official or premises document, such as a council compound notice, licence, tenancy agreement, landlord letter or LHDN, SSM or RMCD letter, by WhatsApp or upload. AI reads it in BM, English or Chinese and extracts each field with its evidence highlighted. A human confirms the dates. Rules then create a deadline, link its consequences (for example, an unpaid compound blocks licence renewal) and route it to the right person, all recorded in the log.
ideas.target_user: Micro and small premises-based businesses (F&B, retail, workshops, salons, clinics), including sole proprietors with no company secretary. The verifiers judged these firms most exposed and least served, because company secretaries mostly cover SSM filings for Sdn Bhd firms. In practice the owner receives the paper and an admin, often a family member, handles it.
ideas.trigger: A document arrives. The owner forwards it to the business's Surat Masuk WhatsApp number (simulated) or uploads it in Orbyte. Synthetic example: Dapur Seri Pelangi Enterprise (fictional; 4 staff; nasi campur shop in Setapak, KL; DBKL licence). On 21 Oct 2026 owner Puan Aini finds a DBKL notice on the shop door. She photographs it and forwards it with: "Irfan, ni surat DBKL dapat pagi tadi kat kedai, tolong tengok apa benda. Kena bayar ke?" The same week, the landlord sends a Chinese-language letter: "租金从2027年1月起调整为每月RM3,500，请于11月15日前续签租约". Every document, notice details and amounts included, is synthetic and made by the team.
ideas.connected_data: (a) The Orbyte premises register: address, DBKL licence number and expiry (31 Dec 2026), signboard licence status. (b) The existing obligation register, Concept 1's Obligation API or a simple built-in list. (c) Orbyte eSign records: if the renewed tenancy is signed there, the both-parties-signed timestamp comes from the audit log and needs no AI. (d) Contacts: landlord, accountant, licensing runner or agent. (e) Previously filed documents for the same premises, used for cross-checks such as an address mismatch or a tenancy ending before the licence period.
ideas.decision_logic: Two layers with a hard boundary between them. Layer 1 (AI, reading only): classify the document type and extract fields, each with its quoted source text and a confidence score. For the notice: issuer DBKL, type compound notice for an advertisement or signboard without a valid licence (the class Sinar Harian reported DBKL issuing on 18 Oct 2024), notice number, date 21 Oct 2026, amount RM300 (synthetic), and a payment window quoted as 'dalam tempoh 14 hari'. For the landlord letter: new rent RM3,500 from 1 Jan 2027 and a renewal deadline of 15 Nov 2026. Layer 2 (deterministic rules, decides consequences): the due date is the notice date plus 14 days, 4 Nov 2026. Because DBKL multi-year renewal requires no outstanding compounds (Utusan, 20 May 2026), the 31 Dec licence renewal becomes BLOCKED until the compound is closed with evidence. A missing signboard licence creates a new 'apply or renew signboard licence' task. The landlord letter creates 'renew tenancy by 15 Nov', plus a stamp-by rule of execution date plus 30 days (Ecovis) that fires when the signed agreement arrives. Exceptions: a field below the confidence threshold, an unknown document type, a premises address that matches nothing in the register, or a due date before the notice date all go to a human 'please confirm' task. Nothing is guessed.
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: In step 2, turning a document into structured fields. A vision-language model reads phone photos taken at an angle, rubber stamps, handwritten dates and mixed BM, English and Chinese text from many issuers: different councils, landlords, LHDN, SSM and RMCD. These do not share fixed templates, so rules or template OCR cannot cope. It also turns relative deadlines ('dalam tempoh 14 hari dari tarikh notis', '收到此函后两周内') into a computable anchor plus an offset, and writes a short plain-language summary of what the document says in the owner's chosen language. AI never decides a consequence or a legal status; layer 2 rules do that, and a human confirms every date.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: The user never converses with it. It is a single-purpose document parser. Its output is a structured record with evidence for each field: a highlighted crop of the photo, the quoted text and a confidence score. A human verifies it field by field, and it then writes to an obligation register and fires routed tasks. The judges see a verification screen and a deadline card, not a chat window. Its nearest relative is Orbyte's own eClaim receipt reader, pointed at a different job.
ideas.human_approval: (1) The owner/proprietor (Puan Aini) confirms the extracted fields before any obligation exists. A due date sets legal exposure, so date and amount fields can never be auto-accepted. She sees the original photo with each field's source text highlighted, the confidence per field, the computed due date and the rule that produced it ('notice date + 14 days per notice text'), the linked consequence ('licence renewal on 31 Dec blocked while this is open', source Utusan 20 May 2026), and a plain BM summary. (2) She chooses and approves the next action: assign Irfan to settle the notice at the counter (no payment is processed in the app), forward it to a licensing agent or the accountant, or record 'disputing with DBKL'. (3) Sharing a document outside the business, for example the tenancy with the landlord's agent for stamping, needs her approval. (4) Closing the obligation needs receipt or evidence uploaded by staff and acceptance by the owner.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: Simulated on Orbyte roles and approval workflow. Owner/Proprietor: views all documents, confirms date and amount fields, approves external sharing, accepts closure. Staff/Admin (Irfan): forwards and uploads documents, can pre-check non-date fields and upload receipts, but cannot confirm dates, share outside the business or close. External helper (accountant, licensing agent, landlord's agent): a guest who sees only the document and obligation shared with them and can upload evidence or comment. Platform operations: sees only model metrics (accuracy, correction rate), never document contents.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The user sees an obligation card: 'DBKL compound, RM300, settle by 4 Nov (10 days)'. It is linked to a red 'Licence renewal 31 Dec: BLOCKED' card and a new 'Signboard licence' task, and the timeline view is updated. Puan Aini gets a WhatsApp message: "Disimpan. Notis kompaun DBKL RM300, tarikh akhir 4 Nov. Irfan ditugaskan. Peringatan 7 hari dan 1 hari sebelum. Pembaharuan lesen Disember ditanda 'tersekat' sehingga resit dimuat naik." The append-only log records: document received (channel, sender, timestamp, file hash); model and prompt version; extracted fields with confidence and quoted spans; human edits as a before/after diff (who and when); the rule applied and its version; the obligation created; sharing approved (to whom, which file); evidence uploaded; closure accepted. The correction rate per field type is aggregated anonymously to monitor accuracy.
ideas.measurable_benefit: ESTIMATES, to be validated. (1) Money kept: the stamping deadline is never missed because it is captured at signing (late penalty from RM50 or 10%, rising to RM100 or 20%; failing to file up to RM10,000, per Ecovis). A forgotten compound no longer silently blocks a DBKL licence renewal (Utusan, 20 May 2026), so the premises stay legally operating. Compound deadlines are visible the day the notice arrives. (2) Time, our estimate: an owner or family admin spends about 15-30 minutes per official document reading it, working out what it is, asking someone and noting the date. Confirming verified fields cuts that to about 2-3 minutes. How many such documents a micro firm receives per month is NOT evidenced; we will measure it in owner interviews. (3) Accuracy, a target and not a result: at least 95% field-level accuracy on dates and amounts on a team-built synthetic set of about 40 documents across 6 types, photographed under poor conditions. We report the measured correction rate honestly in the demo.
ideas.orbyte_fit_and_reuse: It reuses Orbyte's proven document-AI pattern (eClaim already does 'AI receipt reading and policy flags') for business-level statutory and premises documents instead of HR expense claims, so it adds a new capability without duplicating eClaim. It reads eSign (Documenso) audit timestamps, uses the platform approval workflow and audit trail, and writes to a premises and obligation record that feeds the stated 'Business Graph'. It is reusable because document-type schemas are configuration (fields, anchor rules, consequence rules). Adding another council's form or a new letter type means a schema plus a few examples, not code, and the same pipeline serves F&B, retail, workshops and clinics across states. The reusable block is a Document-to-Obligation API: POST /documents returns {type, fields[], evidence[], confidence[]}, and confirmed results are posted to the Obligation API. It is useful to other Orbyte modules and partners, for example an accounting partner receiving structured packs.
ideas.scope_check: Not HR or admin: it handles no employee documents, only business licences, council notices, tenancy agreements and agency letters. No statutory filing: it does not stamp through e-Duti Setem, pay compounds or submit anything; it creates verified deadlines and hand-offs. No real payments: 'settle at counter' is a task, and the receipt is evidence. No legal or financial advice: it summarises what the document says and cites the rule behind each consequence. Questions like 'should I appeal?' or 'am I liable?' route to the named professional. Who stamps a tenancy is flagged for the professional to confirm, because secondary 2026 sources say the duty sits with the lessee by statute but the parties often agree otherwise. PDPA: the demo uses synthetic documents only. In production, documents hold landlord and owner names, IC numbers and addresses. IC numbers are masked in stored fields and originals are encrypted with role-based access. The model provider runs on no-training, minimal-retention terms. Uploaders see a purpose notice. Third-party disclosure needs owner approval and is logged. Retention follows legal minimums (7 years for stamp-duty records, per Ecovis), with deletion on request otherwise.
ideas.prelim_demo_scope: The extraction-and-verification screen, live. Forward or upload a team-made photo of a synthetic DBKL compound notice and a synthetic Chinese-language landlord letter. Show AI fields with highlighted source text and confidence. The owner corrects one low-confidence field. The rules create the 4 Nov deadline and mark the December licence renewal BLOCKED, and the activity log shows the AI extraction, the human edit diff and the approval. Everything else (WhatsApp channel, more document types, eSign link) is roadmap or simulated.
ideas.hardest_risk_and_fallback: Risk: the model misreads or invents a date or amount, producing a wrong deadline, which is worse than none. Fallbacks: (1) No source span, no field: the model must quote the text it read, and an unquoted field stays empty. (2) Every date and amount needs human confirmation, and nothing is auto-accepted. (3) Deterministic cross-checks: the notice date must not be in the future, the due date must be after the notice date, and the address must match the premises register. (4) Below the confidence threshold, a manual entry form opens prefilled beside the photo, which also covers a model or API outage. (5) Measure accuracy on our own synthetic test set and show the number, never claim more. A second risk is frequency: per-firm document volume is unevidenced, so owner interviews before the final must establish it. Roadmap widens intake to utility, insurance and supplier contract documents if volume is low.
ideas.business_model: Usage-based in Orbyte's credit wallet: one credit per document processed, mirroring Orbyte's per-claim and per-signed-document units (Orbyte publishes no RM prices). Freemium: a small monthly free allowance of documents for micro firms. Premium: multi-premises, more document-type packs, a shared inbox for the family or admin team. Partner: accounting firms and licensing agents receive verified, structured packs from many clients and can pay for a partner inbox. The eSign tie-in drives Orbyte eSign usage for tenancy renewals because signing there starts the stamping clock automatically.

ideas.name: Asing: business/personal money splitter for owner-run firms
ideas.one_liner: Every week, Asing reads the owner's mixed personal bank and e-wallet statement together with the WhatsApp order chats. It splits business money from personal money and matches each payment to the order it belongs to. It flags 'dah transfer' claims where the money never arrived. After the owner approves, it locks a clean business ledger that the accountant, and later a lender, can rely on.
ideas.target_user: Micro owner-run businesses (under 5 staff) that take orders on WhatsApp and get paid by DuitNow or e-wallet into the owner's personal account. Examples are home-based F&B, tailoring, beauty, small workshops and online resellers, mostly sole proprietors. KRI/MDEC Discussion Paper 02/26 (24 May 2026) puts micro firms at 70.1% of MSMEs in 2024 and says they 'frequently rely on informal bookkeeping methods or commingle personal and business accounts'. The secondary user is the external bookkeeper or accountant who receives the ledger. KRI's roundtable notes that outsourcing accounting is less feasible for micro firms, so for many of them Asing is the only business record they will have.
ideas.trigger: (1) Scheduled: every Sunday at 9pm, a weekly batch over the last 7 days. (2) Event: the owner uploads a monthly bank e-statement CSV/PDF or an e-wallet export, or a DuitNow credit arrives via the Connect payments connector (simulated). Synthetic example: Dapur Kak Yah Enterprise (fictional), a home kuih and catering business in Seksyen 7, Shah Alam, run by owner Puan Nurhayati and one helper, Mira. For week 43 (19-25 Oct 2026), the batch holds 41 lines from her personal savings account, 12 e-wallet lines and 37 WhatsApp order chats.
ideas.connected_data: All data is synthetic in the demo. (a) Personal bank statement CSV: '21/10 DUITNOW TRF CR 85.00 NUR AISYAH BT HAMDAN kuih'; '22/10 DUITNOW TRF DR 450.00 KEDAI BEKALAN TAN BROS'; '23/10 POS DEBIT PASARAYA SERI MURNI 142.60'; '24/10 TRF DR 300.00 ADIK UITM'; '24/10 DUITNOW TRF CR 50.00 LIM MEI LING'; '25/10 DUITNOW TRF CR 200.00 HAJAH ROS'. (b) E-wallet export. (c) WhatsApp Business chat export (JSON). Examples: 'Aisyah Jiran', 21/10 14:02: 'Kak, nak 2 bekas kuih lapis + karipap 20 biji utk Sabtu. RM85 kan? Dah transfer ya.' Supplier: 'Puan, tepung 5 beg + gula 2 beg + minyak 1 tin, total RM450. Tq.' 'Mei Ling (tadika)': 'Kak, 我要订 50 个 karipap 星期六 pickup, deposit RM50 已经转了.' 'Lina': 'Kak Yah, deposit RM120 utk catering 2 Nov dah tf semalam.' (d) Orbyte Clients list (names, nicknames, phone numbers). (e) The owner's past confirmed decisions and fixed rules. (f) A sector category template (home F&B).
ideas.decision_logic: Step 1, deterministic rules first. Owner fixed rules apply (for example 'ADIK UITM' = personal drawings). An owner-declared split rule applies too (for example, the electricity bill is 30% business because the kitchen is in the home; the owner or accountant sets the percentage, the tool only applies it). An exact match is made when the credit amount equals the agreed order total, the payer name fuzzy-matches a client, and the dates fall within ±3 days. Step 2, AI on the leftovers only. The LLM extracts structured orders from the chats (items, quantity, agreed total, payment claim, date). It then proposes a classification and a match for each unexplained line, with a confidence score and a one-line reason that cites the bank line ID and the chat message ID. Step 3, gating rules. A suggestion with no valid cited IDs is discarded. If confidence is 0.85 or above and the amount is RM300 or less, the item is pre-ticked in the weekly batch. If confidence is below 0.85, the amount is over RM300, or two orders have the same amount on the same day, the item goes to the exception queue. A chat payment claim with no matching credit within 2 days raises a 'claimed paid, not received' flag. Step 4, output. A weekly business ledger: matched sales, business purchases, owner drawings, capital introduced, and unexplained items. Week-43 synthetic results: Aisyah RM85 is matched to her order, Tan Bros RM450 is a business purchase, ADIK RM300 is personal, Mei Ling RM50 is a deposit matched across Chinese and BM text, Lina RM120 is flagged as not received, Hajah Ros RM200 goes to the owner (no chat, could be family), and Seri Murni RM142.60 goes to the owner (ingredients or household shopping).
ideas.where_ai_adds_value: AI is used at Step 2 only. It does three things that rules cannot: (1) Reading informal, mixed-language order chats. Manglish, BM and Chinese with shorthand ('dah tf', 'bekas', '已经转了', 'deposit') hold the agreed total and the payment claim, and no fixed keyword list survives real customer phrasing. (2) Linking bank narrative names to chat identities. 'NUR AISYAH BT HAMDAN' is 'Aisyah Jiran' and 'LIM MEI LING' is 'Mei Ling (tadika)'. These mappings differ for every customer and change all the time. (3) Judging ambiguous merchant lines in context. A RM142.60 supermarket spend in a week with three catering orders and a supplier gap points to ingredients, but only with uncertainty, so it is routed to the owner rather than auto-decided. The rules do the exact matching, thresholds, routing and arithmetic. The AI never posts an entry: it suggests, the rules gate, and the owner approves.
ideas.why_not_a_chatbot: There is no conversation window. Asing is a scheduled batch pipeline over bank lines and chat logs. Its outputs are structured: a ledger, match links, an exception queue with one-tap answers, a lock, and an export to the system of record. The AI is an invisible extraction-and-matching component, held to a strict JSON schema that must cite source IDs. Judges can see it measured as a classifier (precision and recall on a labelled synthetic set), not judged on how fluent its replies are.
ideas.human_approval: (1) The owner (Puan Nurhayati) approves 'Lock Week 43'. That screen shows the weekly totals (synthetic: sales RM2,345.00, business spend RM1,118.60, owner drawings RM300.00). It shows each exception with the bank line and the chat bubble side by side, the AI's reason and confidence, and one-tap buttons 'Bisnes / Peribadi / Pecah (split)'. It also shows the 'claimed paid, not received' list. Locking writes the business entries to the system of record (simulated Connect accounting write-back) and releases them to the accountant. A locked week cannot be edited; reopening it needs the owner and a typed reason. (2) The owner approves any customer-facing message before it goes out. Example draft: 'Hi Lina, Kak Yah belum terima deposit RM120 utk catering 2 Nov. Boleh share resit transfer? Terima kasih.' Nothing is sent automatically, and in the demo sending is simulated.
ideas.roles_and_permissions: All roles are simulated RBAC. Owner: sees all lines, including personal ones. Approves lock and reopen and customer messages, edits rules and split percentages, and grants or revokes accountant access. Helper/staff (Mira): adds orders and notes and tags supplier messages. Sees only the business lines linked to orders she handled. Never sees personal lines, account totals or drawings, and cannot lock. External accountant (Encik Faiz of FZ Akaun & Co, fictional): read-only access to locked business weeks and their evidence. Can export and raise a query on a line, which lands in the owner's exception queue. Cannot see personal lines or edit locked data. AI/system: suggest-only service account; every suggestion is logged. Lenders have no access in this module.
ideas.outcome_and_log: The owner sees a weekly card: 'Minggu 43: Jualan RM2,345 | Belanja bisnes RM1,119 | Ambil peribadi RM300 | 1 bayaran belum masuk: RM120 (Lina)', plus month-to-date business profit and a count of locked weeks ('38 of 43 weeks locked this year'). The accountant sees a clean, locked business ledger with evidence links. The activity log records: import (file hash, line count, who); each rule hit (rule ID); each AI suggestion (model and prompt version, confidence, reason, cited line and message IDs); each owner decision (accept or override, timestamp); lock (period, totals, version hash); write-back to the system of record (returned record IDs); reopen (who, reason); and each customer message approved or sent (simulated).
ideas.measurable_benefit: All figures are estimates unless a source is named. (1) Owner time: an estimated 15-minute weekly review replaces an estimated 4-8 hours of month-end reconstruction. This is a hypothesis to validate with 5 owner interviews. Context: a Lowyat owner thread (6 Mar 2025) says 'The biggest issue is time'.
